questions.q: What color are a robin's eggs?
questions.fact: The color is so famous that robin egg blue is a color name.

questions.q: Which bird is the symbol of wisdom in many stories?
questions.fact: In ancient Greece, the owl was linked with Athena, the goddess of wisdom.

questions.q: How do birds that eat seeds grind their food without teeth?
choices: With a muscular stomach called a gizzard
They swallow seeds whole and never grind them
questions.fact: Many birds swallow tiny stones that help the gizzard grind food.

questions.q: Which animal has blue blood and has barely changed in hundreds of millions of years?
questions.fact: Horseshoe crab blood is used to test medicines for germs.

questions.q: Which animal can regrow its whole body from just a small piece?
questions.fact: Some flatworms called planarians can regrow a whole new body from a tiny piece.

questions.q: Which ocean animal has a body shaped like a disk and a long tail with a stinging spine?
questions.fact: Stingrays are close relatives of sharks and also have skeletons made of cartilage.

questions.q: Which is the largest ray, with fins that can stretch about 7 meters wide?
questions.fact: Manta rays have one of the biggest brains, for their size, of any fish.

questions.q: Which huge deep-sea animal was first photographed alive in the wild in 2004?
questions.fact: Japanese scientists took the photos almost 900 meters deep in the Pacific Ocean.

questions.q: Which sea creature has a spiral shell with many chambers and relatives that go back about 500 million years?
questions.fact: A nautilus moves up and down by changing the amount of gas in its shell chambers.

questions.q: Which spiny round sea animal is a favorite food of sea otters?
questions.fact: Sea urchins move slowly on hundreds of tiny tube feet.

questions.q: Which sea animal can throw out its insides to scare predators and then regrow them?
questions.fact: Some sea cucumbers shoot out sticky threads to tangle up attackers.

questions.q: Which ocean animal makes pearls?
questions.fact: A pearl forms when a mollusk coats a bit of grit or irritation with layers of shiny material.

questions.q: Which tiny ocean creatures are the main food of many whales, penguins and seals in the Southern Ocean?
questions.fact: Antarctic krill are among the most plentiful animals on Earth, with hundreds of trillions of them.

questions.q: What is plankton?
choices: Tiny living things that drift in water
questions.fact: Plankton made by tiny ocean plants produce a large share of the oxygen we breathe.

questions.q: Which fish can glide above the water for long distances using big fins like wings?
questions.fact: Flying fish can glide for about 200 meters by leaping out of the water.

questions.q: Which fish has a long, flat, sword-like bill?
questions.fact: Swordfish can heat their eyes and brains to see better in cold, deep water.

questions.q: Which fish is the heaviest bony fish in the world?
questions.fact: An ocean sunfish, also called a mola, can weigh more than 2,000 kilograms.

questions.q: Which fish can live out of water and even climb onto mangrove roots?
questions.fact: Mudskippers breathe through their skin and through water they hold in their gill chambers.

questions.q: What is a male deer called?
questions.fact: A female deer is called a doe.

questions.q: What is a male sheep called?
questions.fact: A female sheep is called a ewe.

questions.q: What is a female horse called?
questions.fact: An adult male horse is called a stallion.

questions.q: What is a male chicken called?
questions.fact: Roosters crow at many times of the day, not only at sunrise.

questions.q: What is a female pig called?
questions.fact: A male pig is called a boar.

questions.q: What is a male duck called?
questions.fact: Many male ducks have bright colors, while females are brown to stay hidden on the nest.

questions.q: What is a male goose called?
questions.fact: A female goose is simply called a goose.

questions.q: Which type of animal is the axolotl, which is often called a Mexican walking fish?
questions.fact: Axolotls usually keep their feathery gills and live in water their whole lives.

questions.q: Which animal can jump the highest compared to its body size?
questions.fact: A flea can jump more than 100 times its own body length.

questions.q: How far can a red kangaroo jump in a single hop?
questions.fact: Kangaroos cannot easily walk backward.

questions.q: What does a kangaroo use its strong tail for?
choices: Balance and support, like a fifth leg
questions.fact: When moving slowly, a kangaroo leans on its tail while it swings its legs forward.

questions.q: Which animal has a nose like a short trunk and lives in rainforests of South America and Asia?
questions.fact: Baby tapirs have stripes and spots that fade as they grow.

questions.q: Which cat has a very short tail and tufted ears and lives in northern forests?
questions.fact: Lynx have huge, furry paws that work like snowshoes.

questions.q: Which wild cat of the Americas is also called a cougar, puma or mountain lion?
questions.fact: It holds the record for the animal with the most common names in English.

questions.q: Which small wild cat of North America is named for its short tail?
questions.fact: Bobcats are about twice the size of a pet cat.

questions.q: Which wild African cat has very long legs and big ears to hear prey in tall grass?
questions.fact: Servals can leap high into the air to catch birds.

questions.q: Which weasel relative is famous for being fearless and fighting much bigger animals?
questions.fact: Honey badgers have thick, loose skin that makes them hard to grab.

questions.q: Which animal is famous for washing its food in water before eating?
questions.fact: Raccoons are actually feeling their food, since wet paws are extra sensitive.

questions.q: Which animal is red, fluffy and lives in the Himalayas, though it is not a bear?
questions.fact: Red pandas were named pandas before giant pandas were.

questions.q: Which fox lives in the Sahara Desert and has huge ears?
questions.fact: Its big ears help it hear prey underground and also give off heat to stay cool.

questions.q: Which tiny primate has eyes so big that each one is about as large as its brain?
questions.fact: Tarsiers cannot move their eyes, so they turn their heads instead, like owls.

questions.q: Which wild pig of Africa has warts on its face?
questions.fact: Warthogs kneel on their front knees when they eat grass.

questions.q: Which antelope can leap about 3 meters high and is common in African savannas?
questions.fact: When running from danger, impalas leap in many directions to confuse predators.

questions.q: Which large animal of Africa travels with zebras in a giant migration each year?
questions.fact: More than a million wildebeest travel across the Serengeti and Masai Mara each year.

questions.q: Which animal has the thickest skin of any land mammal?
questions.fact: Rhino skin can be about 5 centimeters thick in places.

questions.q: Which rhinoceros is the largest kind?
questions.fact: Both white and black rhinos are actually gray.

questions.q: Which animal is the national animal of Australia, along with the emu?
questions.fact: The kangaroo and emu both appear on Australia's coat of arms.

questions.q: Which animal is the national animal of China?
questions.fact: Giant pandas have been sent to zoos in other countries as signs of friendship.

questions.q: Which animal on the endangered list was saved partly because the United States banned the pesticide DDT?
questions.fact: DDT made eggshells so thin they broke before hatching.

questions.q: Which ape is critically endangered and lives in the mountains of Rwanda, Uganda and Congo?
questions.fact: As of 2025, there are only about 1,000 mountain gorillas, but their numbers have been slowly growing.

questions.q: What kind of fish is Nemo in the movie Finding Nemo?
questions.fact: All clownfish are born male, and some later change into females.

questions.q: Which cartoon character from Finding Nemo is a blue tang?
questions.fact: Blue tangs have sharp spines near their tails for defense.

questions.q: Which pet fish was first kept by people in ancient China?
questions.fact: Goldfish come from a wild carp and were bred in China over a thousand years ago.

questions.q: Which fish is also called the Siamese fighting fish?
questions.fact: Male bettas build nests out of bubbles on the water's surface.

questions.q: Which pet reptile is a popular lizard from Australia known for its spiky beard?
questions.fact: Bearded dragons puff out and darken their beards when they feel threatened.

questions.q: Which bird's heart can beat more than 1,000 times a minute?
questions.fact: Hummingbirds burn so much energy that they must feed many times every hour.

questions.q: Which group of animals has the most known species?
questions.fact: Scientists have named about a million insect species, and there are many more to find.

questions.q: Which insect is famous for its praying pose and for catching other insects with spiky front legs?
questions.fact: A praying mantis can turn its head almost all the way around to look behind it.

questions.q: Which insect makes a big ball-shaped paper nest from chewed wood?
questions.fact: Wasps were making paper long before people learned how.

questions.q: Which insect sense organ helps ants and moths smell?
questions.fact: Some male moths can smell a female from kilometers away with their feathery antennae.

questions.q: How many eyes do most spiders have?
questions.fact: Jumping spiders have two huge front eyes that give them sharp vision.

questions.q: How many bones is a newborn baby born with?
questions.fact: Many of a baby's bones fuse together as the child grows, leaving 206 in adults.

questions.q: What is the smallest bone in the human body called?
questions.fact: The stapes, or stirrup, is about 3 millimeters long and sits in the middle ear.

questions.q: What is the common name for the patella?
questions.fact: The kneecap protects the front of the knee joint.

questions.q: What is the common name for the clavicle?
questions.fact: The collarbone is one of the most commonly broken bones.

questions.q: What is the common name for the sternum?
questions.fact: The ribs connect to the breastbone at the front of the chest.

questions.q: What is the common name for the scapula?
questions.fact: The shoulder blade is a flat, triangle-shaped bone on your upper back.

questions.q: What is the common name for the coccyx?
questions.fact: The tailbone is made of a few small bones fused together.

questions.q: What is the only bone in the skull that can move?
questions.fact: The lower jaw is called the mandible.

questions.q: How many pairs of ribs do most people have?
questions.fact: A small number of people have an extra rib.

questions.q: What do we call the bones that make up the spine?
questions.fact: Most adults have 33 vertebrae, though some fuse together.

questions.q: What are the bones in your fingers and toes called?
questions.fact: Each finger has three phalanges, while each thumb has two.

questions.q: About how many bones are in one human hand, including the wrist?
questions.fact: Your two hands and wrists together have over a quarter of all your bones.

questions.q: What is the soft tissue inside many bones that makes blood cells called?
questions.fact: Bone marrow makes billions of new blood cells every day.

questions.q: What mineral makes bones hard and strong?
questions.fact: Milk, yogurt, cheese and leafy greens are good sources of calcium.

questions.q: What is the bendy tissue in your nose and ears called?
questions.fact: Cartilage also cushions the ends of bones in your joints.

questions.q: What connects bones to other bones at a joint?
questions.fact: Ligaments are tough bands that keep joints steady.

questions.q: What kind of joint is your shoulder?
questions.fact: Ball and socket joints let your arm swing in a full circle.

questions.q: What kind of joint is your knee?
questions.fact: Like a door hinge, your knee mostly bends in one direction.

questions.q: What kind of joint lets you shake your head no?
questions.fact: The pivot joint is between the top two bones of your neck.

questions.q: What is the name for a broken bone?
questions.fact: Broken bones heal by growing new bone tissue across the break.

questions.q: What is a sprain?
questions.fact: Ankles are the most commonly sprained joint.

questions.q: About how many muscles are in the human body?
questions.fact: Muscles make up roughly a third to two fifths of your body weight.

questions.q: What is the largest muscle in the human body?
questions.fact: The gluteus maximus is in your buttocks and helps you stand up and climb.

questions.q: What are the three types of muscle in the body?
questions.fact: Cardiac muscle is found only in the heart.

questions.q: Which type of muscle is found only in the heart?
questions.fact: Cardiac muscle never gets tired the way arm muscles do.

questions.q: What do we call muscles you can control on purpose, like in your arms?
questions.fact: Muscles in your stomach and blood vessels work without you thinking about them.

questions.q: What muscle is on the front of your upper arm?
questions.fact: The triceps on the back of the arm straightens your elbow.

questions.q: What large muscle group is on the front of your thigh?
questions.fact: Quadriceps means four heads, because it is made of four muscles.

questions.q: Which muscle under your lungs helps you breathe?
questions.fact: Hiccups are sudden spasms of the diaphragm.

questions.q: What are muscles in the body able to do?
questions.fact: Muscles work in pairs, one pulling one way and its partner pulling back.

questions.q: Which tendon at the back of your heel is the strongest in the body?
questions.fact: It is named after Achilles, a Greek hero whose heel was his only weak spot.

questions.q: What do we call the tiny tubes that connect arteries and veins?
questions.fact: Some capillaries are so thin that red blood cells pass through them one at a time.

questions.q: Which blood vessels carry blood back to the heart?
questions.fact: Veins have valves that keep blood from flowing backward.

questions.q: What is the largest artery in the body?
questions.fact: The aorta carries blood out of the heart to the rest of the body.

questions.q: About how long would all your blood vessels stretch if laid end to end?
questions.fact: That is long enough to wrap around Earth more than twice.

questions.q: About how much blood does an adult have?
questions.fact: A child has less, depending on their size.

questions.q: About how many times does a resting adult heart beat each minute?
questions.fact: Children's hearts usually beat a bit faster than adults'.

questions.q: What is the liquid part of blood called?
questions.fact: Plasma is mostly water and makes up a little more than half of your blood.

questions.q: Which tiny blood cell pieces help blood clot when you get a cut?
questions.fact: Platelets stick together to plug the cut, then help form a scab.

questions.q: What color is human blood inside your body?
questions.fact: Veins look blue through the skin because of how light passes through skin, but the blood inside is dark red.

questions.q: What makes red blood cells red?
questions.fact: When hemoglobin picks up oxygen, it turns a brighter red.

questions.q: About how long does a red blood cell live?
questions.fact: Your body makes millions of new red blood cells every second.

questions.q: What are the four main blood types?
questions.fact: Each type can also be positive or negative.

questions.q: Which blood type is often called the universal donor?
questions.fact: In emergencies, O negative blood can be given to almost anyone.

questions.q: Who discovered the main human blood groups in 1901?
questions.fact: Knowing blood types made blood transfusions much safer.

questions.q: Which scientist showed in 1628 that the heart pumps blood around the body in a circle?
questions.fact: Before Harvey, many people thought the liver made new blood all the time.

questions.q: What do we call the pressure of blood pushing on artery walls?
questions.fact: Doctors measure blood pressure with an inflatable cuff around your arm.

questions.q: What can you feel at your wrist or neck that shows your heartbeat?
questions.fact: You can count your pulse for 15 seconds and multiply by 4 to find your heart rate.

questions.q: What tool do doctors use to listen to your heart and lungs?
questions.fact: The stethoscope was invented in France in 1816.

questions.q: What do heart valves do?
choices: Keep blood flowing in one direction
questions.fact: The lub-dub sound of a heartbeat is made by valves closing.

questions.q: Which side of the heart pumps blood to the lungs?
questions.fact: The left side pumps oxygen-rich blood out to the rest of the body.

questions.q: About how big is your heart?
choices: About the size of your head
About the size of a pea
About the size of a football
About the size of your fist
questions.fact: Your heart beats more than 100,000 times a day.

questions.q: What are the tiny air sacs in the lungs called?
questions.fact: Lungs have hundreds of millions of alveoli, where oxygen passes into the blood.

questions.q: What is the tube that carries air from your throat to your lungs called?
questions.fact: The trachea is also called the windpipe and has rings of cartilage to keep it open.

questions.q: What gas do you breathe out that your body needs to get rid of?
questions.fact: Your cells make carbon dioxide when they turn food into energy.

questions.q: What is the voice box called?
questions.fact: Your vocal cords sit inside the larynx and vibrate to make sound.

questions.q: Which lung is a little smaller?
questions.fact: The left lung is smaller to make room for the heart.

questions.q: What is the flap that covers your windpipe when you swallow called?
questions.fact: When food goes down the wrong way, it is because the epiglottis did not close in time.

questions.q: What is the little dangly thing at the back of your throat called?
questions.fact: The uvula helps close off your nose when you swallow.

questions.q: What makes you yawn?
choices: Scientists are still not completely sure
questions.fact: Yawning is contagious, and even reading about it can make you yawn.

questions.q: What is a sneeze?
choices: A type of cough from the stomach
A sign of a broken bone
A reflex to clear your nose of irritants
questions.fact: A sneeze can blast air out at high speed, so cover it with your elbow.

questions.q: What is the largest internal organ in the body?
questions.fact: The liver can regrow when part of it is removed.

questions.q: Which organ makes bile to help digest fats?
questions.fact: Bile is stored in a small organ called the gallbladder.

questions.q: Which organ makes insulin to control blood sugar?
questions.fact: People with type 1 diabetes have a pancreas that does not make enough insulin.

questions.q: Which organ helps filter blood and fight infections and sits on the left side under the ribs?
questions.fact: People can live without a spleen, but they may get some infections more easily.

questions.q: Which small, finger-shaped pouch is attached to the large intestine?
questions.fact: When the appendix gets infected, it is called appendicitis and is often removed.

questions.q: Which organ stores urine until you go to the bathroom?
questions.fact: An adult bladder can hold about half a liter.

questions.q: What do we call the tubes that carry urine from the kidneys to the bladder?
questions.fact: Each kidney has its own ureter.

questions.q: About how big is a kidney?
choices: About the size of a fist
About the size of a pea
About the size of a basketball
About the size of a car tire
questions.fact: Kidneys are shaped like beans, which is why some beans are called kidney beans.

questions.q: Can a person live with only one kidney?
questions.fact: Many people donate one kidney to someone who needs it.

questions.q: How long is the small intestine in an adult?
questions.fact: It is called small because it is narrow, not short.

questions.q: What are the tiny finger-like bumps lining the small intestine called?
questions.fact: Villi give the intestine a huge surface for soaking up food.

questions.q: What does the large intestine mainly do?
questions.fact: Trillions of helpful bacteria live in the large intestine.

questions.q: What liquid in your mouth starts breaking down food?
questions.fact: You make roughly a liter of saliva every day.

questions.q: What strong acid is in your stomach?
questions.fact: A thick layer of mucus keeps stomach acid from digesting your stomach itself.

questions.q: About how long does it take food to travel all the way through your digestive system?
questions.fact: Food usually spends a few hours in the stomach.

questions.q: What is the wave-like squeezing that moves food through your digestive system called?
questions.fact: Peristalsis works even if you are upside down.

questions.q: What are the proteins in your body that speed up digestion called?
questions.fact: Each enzyme does one special job, like breaking down starch or protein.

questions.q: What causes the rumbling sound in your stomach?
choices: Gas and liquid moving through your intestines
questions.fact: The scientific name for a tummy rumble is borborygmi.

questions.q: What is the largest part of the brain?
questions.fact: The cerebrum handles thinking, memory, speaking and movement.

questions.q: Which part of the brain helps control balance and coordination?
questions.fact: Cerebellum means little brain in Latin.

questions.q: Which part of the brain controls breathing and heartbeat?
questions.fact: The brain stem connects the brain to the spinal cord.

questions.q: Which side of the brain mainly controls the right side of the body?
questions.fact: The nerves cross over, so each half of the brain controls the opposite side of the body.

questions.q: About how much does an adult brain weigh?
questions.fact: The brain is about 2 percent of your body weight but uses about 20 percent of your energy.

questions.q: What are nerve cells called?
questions.fact: Your brain has about 86 billion neurons.

questions.q: How fast can signals travel along some nerves?
questions.fact: Fast nerve signals let you jerk your hand away from something hot almost instantly.

questions.q: What do we call a quick automatic movement, like jerking your hand away from something hot?
questions.fact: Some reflexes are handled by the spinal cord before the signal even reaches your brain.

questions.q: What happens when a doctor taps just below your kneecap?
choices: Your leg kicks out by reflex
questions.fact: This is called the knee-jerk reflex.

questions.q: What is the brain's fluid cushion called?
questions.fact: This clear fluid helps protect the brain from bumps.

questions.q: What are the folds and grooves on the brain's surface for?
choices: They pack more brain into the skull
questions.fact: If you could flatten out the brain's outer layer, it would be about the size of a pillowcase.

questions.q: Which part of the eye controls how much light enters by changing size?
questions.fact: Your pupils get bigger in the dark and smaller in bright light.

questions.q: What is the layer at the back of the eye that senses light?
questions.fact: The retina has millions of light-sensing cells called rods and cones.

questions.q: Which cells in your eyes help you see colors?
questions.fact: Most people have three types of cones, for red, green and blue light.

questions.q: Which cells in your eyes help you see in dim light?
questions.fact: Rods do not see color, which is why things look gray in very dim light.

questions.q: What is the clear front window of the eye called?
questions.fact: The cornea has no blood vessels and gets oxygen straight from the air.

questions.q: Which nerve carries signals from the eye to the brain?
questions.fact: Where the optic nerve leaves the eye, there is a blind spot with no light sensors.

questions.q: Does the image on your retina appear upside down?
choices: Yes, and your brain flips it
questions.fact: The lens of your eye bends light so the image lands upside down.

questions.q: What is it called when someone cannot tell certain colors apart, like red and green?
questions.fact: Color blindness is much more common in boys than in girls.

questions.q: What kind of glasses help people who cannot see faraway things clearly?
questions.fact: Being nearsighted means you see near things clearly but faraway things look blurry.

questions.q: Why do your eyes blink?
choices: To keep them moist and clean
questions.fact: Most people blink about 15 to 20 times a minute.

questions.q: What do tears do besides show feelings?
choices: Keep eyes wet and wash away dust
questions.fact: Tears also contain substances that fight germs.

questions.q: What are the three tiny bones in the middle ear?
questions.fact: Their scientific names are the malleus, incus and stapes.

questions.q: What is the snail-shaped part of the inner ear that helps you hear?
questions.fact: Tiny hair cells in the cochlea turn sound vibrations into nerve signals.

questions.q: What part of your body helps you keep your balance besides your eyes?
questions.fact: Fluid moving in your inner ear tells your brain how your head is moving.

questions.q: Why do you feel dizzy after spinning around?
choices: Fluid in your inner ear keeps moving after you stop
questions.fact: Your brain gets mixed signals from your eyes and inner ear.

questions.q: What thin layer of skin in the ear vibrates when sound hits it?
questions.fact: The eardrum passes vibrations on to the tiny bones of the middle ear.

questions.q: Why do your ears pop on an airplane?
choices: Air pressure inside and outside your ear evens out
questions.fact: Swallowing or yawning helps your ears pop.

questions.q: What is earwax for?
choices: Protecting and cleaning the ear canal
questions.fact: Doctors say you should not push cotton swabs deep into your ears.

questions.q: About how many taste buds does a person have?
questions.fact: Taste buds are replaced about every one to two weeks.

questions.q: What are the five basic tastes?
choices: Hot, cold, wet, dry and soft
Sweet, salty, sour, bitter and umami
Sweet, spicy, crunchy, salty and sour
Red, green, blue, yellow and white
questions.fact: Umami is a savory taste found in foods like cheese, mushrooms and broth.

questions.q: Why does food taste bland when you have a cold?
choices: Much of flavor comes from your sense of smell
questions.fact: Holding your nose while eating shows how much smell matters for flavor.

questions.q: Is spicy heat from chili peppers a taste?
choices: No, it is a feeling of pain or heat
Yes, it is the sixth taste
Yes, it is a sweet taste
Only on the back of the tongue
questions.fact: A chemical in chili peppers called capsaicin tricks heat sensors in your mouth.

questions.q: Is the idea of a tongue map, with each taste in one area, correct?
choices: Yes, sweet is only at the tip
Yes, bitter is only on the sides
No, all areas of the tongue can sense all tastes
questions.fact: The tongue map myth came from a mistranslation of a German paper from 1901.

questions.q: About how many different smells can a human nose tell apart?
questions.fact: Some scientists think people may be able to detect over a trillion different smells.

questions.q: What is the name of the sense that tells you where your body parts are without looking?
questions.fact: It is why you can touch your nose with your eyes closed.

questions.q: What sense organ is your skin?
choices: It is not a sense organ
questions.fact: Your fingertips have some of the most touch sensors in your body.

questions.q: What is the outer layer of your skin called?
questions.fact: You shed tens of thousands of dead skin cells every minute.

questions.q: What gives skin its color?
questions.fact: Melanin also helps protect skin from the Sun's ultraviolet rays.

questions.q: What are freckles?
questions.fact: Freckles often get darker in summer after time in the sun.

questions.q: Why do you get goosebumps?
choices: Tiny muscles pull your hairs upright
questions.fact: In furry animals, raising the hair helps them stay warm or look bigger.

questions.q: Why do you sweat?
questions.fact: As sweat evaporates, it carries heat away from your skin.

questions.q: About how many sweat glands does a person have?
questions.fact: The palms of your hands and soles of your feet have the most.

questions.q: Why do your fingers get wrinkly in the bath?
choices: They soak up so much water they burst
Your nervous system makes them wrinkle
questions.fact: Scientists think wrinkly fingers may help grip wet things better.

questions.q: What are fingernails and hair made of?
questions.fact: Animal claws, hooves and horns are made of keratin too.

questions.q: Which grow faster, fingernails or toenails?
choices: They grow at the same speed
questions.fact: Fingernails grow about 3 millimeters a month.

questions.q: About how many hairs are on a person's head?
questions.fact: People with blond hair usually have more hairs on their heads than people with red hair.

questions.q: About how many hairs does a person normally lose each day?
questions.fact: New hairs grow back to replace the ones that fall out.

questions.q: Which part of the hair is alive?
questions.fact: The hair you can see is made of dead cells, so cutting it does not hurt.

questions.q: What makes fingerprints special?
choices: No two people have the same ones
questions.fact: Even identical twins have different fingerprints.

questions.q: At what age do most people's fingerprints form?
questions.fact: Fingerprints form in the womb, months before birth.

questions.q: What causes a bruise?
choices: Blood leaking from tiny broken vessels under the skin
questions.fact: Bruises change colors from purple to green to yellow as they heal.

questions.q: What is a scab?
choices: A dried blood clot that protects a cut while it heals
questions.fact: Picking scabs can slow healing and may leave a scar.

questions.q: What is the soft inside of a tooth with nerves and blood vessels called?
questions.fact: A toothache often happens when decay reaches the pulp.

questions.q: How many teeth does an adult usually have, including wisdom teeth?
questions.fact: Many people have their wisdom teeth removed because there is not enough room.

questions.q: What are the pointy teeth next to the front teeth called?
questions.fact: Canines are named after dogs, which have big pointy canine teeth.

questions.q: What are the flat front teeth used for biting called?
questions.fact: You have eight incisors, four on top and four on bottom.

questions.q: What are the big flat teeth at the back used for grinding food called?
questions.fact: Molar comes from the Latin word for millstone, a stone used to grind grain.

questions.q: What sticky film of germs on teeth causes cavities?
questions.fact: Bacteria in plaque eat sugar and make acid that wears away enamel.

questions.q: What should you use to clean between your teeth?
questions.fact: Floss reaches places a toothbrush cannot.

questions.q: At about what age do most kids start losing baby teeth?
questions.fact: The front teeth are usually the first to fall out.

questions.q: What is the body's system of glands that make hormones called?
questions.fact: Hormones are chemical messengers that travel in the blood.

questions.q: Which gland in the brain is sometimes called the master gland?
questions.fact: The pituitary gland is only about the size of a pea.

questions.q: Which hormone gives you a burst of energy when you are scared?
questions.fact: Adrenaline makes your heart pound and gets your body ready to fight or run.

questions.q: Which hormone helps make you sleepy when it gets dark?
questions.fact: Bright screens at night can lower melatonin and make it harder to fall asleep.

questions.q: Which gland in the neck controls how fast your body uses energy?
questions.fact: The thyroid is shaped a bit like a butterfly.

questions.q: What hormone tells your body to grow taller as a kid?
questions.fact: Much of your growth hormone is released while you sleep.

questions.q: What is the body's defense system against germs called?
questions.fact: Your immune system remembers germs it has fought before.

questions.q: What proteins does your immune system make to attack specific germs?
questions.fact: Vaccines teach your body to make antibodies without getting sick first.

questions.q: Why do you get a fever when you are sick?
choices: Your body heats up to help fight germs
questions.fact: A normal body temperature is about 37 degrees Celsius.

questions.q: What is the normal human body temperature, about?
questions.fact: That is about 98.6 degrees Fahrenheit, though normal can vary a little from person to person.

questions.q: What do vaccines do?
choices: Kill all bacteria in your body
Train your immune system to recognize a germ
questions.fact: Vaccines have prevented millions of deaths from diseases like measles and polio.

questions.q: What are the small bean-shaped lumps that filter germs and can swell when you are sick?
questions.fact: Swollen lymph nodes in your neck often mean your body is fighting an infection.

questions.q: What are the two lumps at the back of your throat that help fight germs?
questions.fact: Tonsils sometimes get infected and swollen, which is called tonsillitis.

questions.q: What is an allergy?
choices: When the immune system overreacts to something harmless
questions.fact: Pollen, peanuts and pet dander are common things people are allergic to.

questions.q: What is the common cold caused by?
questions.fact: Going outside with wet hair does not give you a cold, but germs from other people can.

questions.q: Why don't antibiotics cure colds?
choices: Colds are caused by viruses, and antibiotics only kill bacteria
questions.fact: Rest, fluids and time are the usual cure for colds.

questions.q: What is the best way to stop germs spreading when you cough?
choices: Hold your breath for a minute
Cough into your elbow or a tissue
questions.fact: Then wash your hands with soap and water.

questions.q: How long should you scrub your hands with soap?
questions.fact: That is about how long it takes to hum Happy Birthday twice.

questions.q: About how many cells are in the human body?
questions.fact: Red blood cells make up most of them by number.

questions.q: Which are the biggest cells in the human body?
questions.fact: A human egg cell is just barely big enough to see without a microscope.

questions.q: What is the longest cell in the human body?
choices: A nerve cell running down the leg
questions.fact: Some nerve cells stretch from the bottom of the spine to the toes, about a meter long.

questions.q: What carries the instructions that make you look like your family?
questions.fact: You get half of your DNA from each parent.

questions.q: How many chromosomes do most humans have in each cell?
questions.fact: Chromosomes come in 23 pairs.

questions.q: What is the name for twins that come from one egg and share almost the same DNA?
questions.fact: Fraternal twins come from two different eggs and are no more alike than other siblings.

questions.q: What do we call a feature, like eye color, that is passed from parents to children?
questions.fact: Freckles, dimples and earlobe shape can all be inherited traits.

questions.q: What are the six main types of nutrients your body needs?
choices: Sugar, salt, candy, chips, soda and water
Carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals and water
questions.fact: A balanced diet gives your body all six.

questions.q: What is the main job of carbohydrates in food?
questions.fact: Bread, rice, pasta and fruit are full of carbohydrates.

questions.q: What is the main job of protein in your diet?
questions.fact: Beans, eggs, fish, meat and nuts are good sources of protein.

questions.q: Which vitamin helps your eyes see in dim light?
questions.fact: Carrots, sweet potatoes and spinach contain the building blocks for vitamin A.

questions.q: Which vitamin helps your blood clot?
questions.fact: Leafy green vegetables like kale and spinach are full of vitamin K.

questions.q: Which disease did sailors get long ago from not eating enough vitamin C?
questions.fact: British sailors were given limes to prevent it, which is why they were nicknamed limeys.

questions.q: Which disease, causing soft and bent bones, comes from not getting enough vitamin D?
questions.fact: Sunlight and foods like fish and fortified milk help prevent rickets.

questions.q: Which mineral helps your blood carry oxygen?
questions.fact: Not getting enough iron can make people feel tired, a condition called anemia.

questions.q: What fiber-rich foods help keep your digestion moving smoothly?
questions.fact: Fiber is a part of plants that your body cannot fully digest.

questions.q: About what fraction of the human body is water?
questions.fact: Babies have an even higher percentage of water than adults.

questions.q: About how long can a person survive without water?
questions.fact: In hot weather, the body loses water even faster.

questions.q: What is it called when your body does not have enough water?
questions.fact: Dark yellow urine and headaches can be signs you need to drink more water.

questions.q: What is a calorie?
choices: A unit of the energy in food
questions.fact: Kids who are active need more food energy than kids who sit a lot.

questions.q: What happens to extra food energy your body does not use right away?
choices: Much of it is stored as fat
questions.fact: Fat stores energy and also keeps your body warm.

questions.q: About how many hours of sleep do kids aged 6 to 12 need each night?
questions.fact: Sleep helps your brain store memories and your body grow.

questions.q: What is the stage of sleep when you dream the most called?
questions.fact: REM stands for rapid eye movement, because your eyes dart around under your eyelids.

questions.q: What happens to your muscles during REM sleep?
choices: Most of them become very relaxed and still
questions.fact: This stops you from acting out your dreams.

questions.q: What happens to your brain while you sleep?
questions.fact: Getting good sleep before a test can help you remember what you studied.

questions.q: Why does your stomach growl when you are hungry?
choices: Your stomach and intestines squeeze even when empty
questions.fact: The sounds are louder when your stomach is empty because there is nothing to muffle them.

questions.q: What is the medical name for the hiccups?
questions.fact: Hiccups happen when your diaphragm suddenly tightens and your vocal cords snap shut.

questions.q: What causes brain freeze when you eat something cold too fast?
choices: Blood vessels in your mouth and head reacting to the cold
questions.fact: Pressing your tongue against the roof of your mouth can help it go away faster.

questions.q: What is the funny bone?
choices: A nerve at your elbow, not a bone
questions.fact: Bumping the ulnar nerve against bone gives that tingly zap.

questions.q: Why does your foot fall asleep?
choices: Pressure squeezes nerves and blood vessels
questions.fact: The pins and needles feeling goes away when the pressure is gone.

questions.q: What is the body's largest gland?
questions.fact: The liver does more than 500 jobs, like cleaning blood and storing energy.

questions.q: What is the strongest muscle in the body based on its weight?
questions.fact: Your jaw muscles can bite down with surprising force.

questions.q: What is the hardest working muscle in the body?
questions.fact: The heart beats about 2.5 billion times over an average lifetime.

questions.q: What are the two bones in your lower leg?
questions.fact: The tibia, or shin bone, is the larger of the two.

questions.q: What are the two bones in your forearm?
questions.fact: The radius is on the thumb side of your arm.

questions.q: What is the bone in your upper arm called?
questions.fact: Its name sounds like humorous, which is one reason people call the elbow nerve the funny bone.

questions.q: What bones form your hips?
questions.fact: The pelvis is shaped like a bowl and supports your upper body.

questions.q: What is the name of the bone that protects the brain from the front, at the forehead?
questions.fact: The skull is made of many bones joined together by wavy seams called sutures.

questions.q: What are the soft spots on a baby's head called?
questions.fact: The soft spots let the skull squeeze a little during birth and let the brain grow.

questions.q: What happens to astronauts' bones in space?
questions.fact: Exercise helps astronauts slow down bone loss.

questions.q: What do bones do besides holding you up?
choices: Protect organs, make blood cells and store minerals
questions.fact: Bones are living tissue that can grow and heal.

questions.q: What is the main job of the skeletal system?
questions.fact: Without a skeleton, your body would collapse like a jellyfish.

questions.q: Which body system carries oxygen and nutrients around the body?
questions.fact: The circulatory system includes the heart, blood and blood vessels.

questions.q: Which body system breaks down food into nutrients?
questions.fact: The digestive system includes the mouth, stomach and intestines.

questions.q: Which body system includes the lungs and windpipe?
questions.fact: The respiratory system brings in oxygen and gets rid of carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Which body system removes liquid waste from the blood?
questions.fact: The kidneys filter about 150 liters of blood every day.

questions.q: Which body system includes the skin, hair and nails?
questions.fact: Integument means a covering.

questions.q: About how much does an adult's skin weigh?
questions.fact: That makes skin heavier than any single internal organ.

questions.q: What helps keep skin safe from sunburn?
questions.fact: Sunscreen should be put on again every couple of hours outside.

questions.q: What is the condition called when the body gets dangerously hot?
questions.fact: Rest in the shade, drink water and get help if someone shows signs of heatstroke.

questions.q: What is it called when the body gets dangerously cold?
questions.fact: Shivering is your body's way of making heat by moving muscles quickly.

questions.q: What is frostbite?
choices: Freezing of skin and tissue in extreme cold
A bite from a winter insect
questions.fact: Fingers, toes, ears and noses are most at risk of frostbite.

questions.q: Why do you shiver when you are cold?
questions.fact: Shivering can increase the heat your body makes several times over.

questions.q: Why does your face turn red when you are embarrassed or hot?
choices: Blood vessels near the skin widen
questions.fact: This helps your body release heat.

questions.q: What do your kidneys make from waste and extra water?
questions.fact: Your kidneys clean all your blood many times every day.

questions.q: What is the yellow color in urine from?
choices: A substance made when old red blood cells break down
questions.fact: Drinking more water makes urine lighter in color.

questions.q: What does the gallbladder store?
questions.fact: People can live without a gallbladder.

questions.q: What organ do you use to think?
questions.fact: Ancient Egyptians thought the heart did the thinking and threw away the brain during mummification.

questions.q: Can you live without your appendix?
choices: Only if you are an adult
questions.fact: Scientists think the appendix may store helpful gut bacteria.

questions.q: How many lungs do people have?
questions.fact: Together, your lungs have a surface area about the size of half a tennis court.

questions.q: About how many breaths does a resting adult take per minute?
questions.fact: Kids usually breathe a bit faster than adults.

questions.q: What happens to your heart rate when you exercise?
questions.fact: Exercise makes your heart stronger over time.

questions.q: Why is regular exercise good for your body?
choices: It strengthens your heart, lungs, muscles and bones
It stops you from needing sleep
questions.fact: Kids should aim for about an hour of active play every day.

questions.q: What happens to muscles when you exercise them often?
questions.fact: Tiny tears in muscle fibers repair and grow back stronger.

questions.q: What causes the sore feeling in muscles a day or two after hard exercise?
choices: Tiny muscle fiber damage being repaired
questions.fact: Soreness usually goes away in a few days.

questions.q: What is a cramp?
choices: A sudden, painful tightening of a muscle
questions.fact: Stretching the muscle gently can help a cramp go away.

questions.q: What is the heel bone called?
questions.fact: The heel bone is the largest bone in the foot.

questions.q: How many bones are in one human foot?
questions.fact: Your two feet together have 52 bones, about a quarter of all your bones.

questions.q: What is the arch of your foot for?
choices: Absorbing shock and helping you walk
questions.fact: The arch acts like a spring with every step.

questions.q: What are the tough, thick patches of skin that form from rubbing called?
questions.fact: Guitar players often get calluses on their fingertips.

questions.q: What is a blister?
choices: A bubble of fluid under the skin from rubbing or burns
questions.fact: The fluid protects the skin underneath while it heals.

questions.q: What is the white part of your eye called?
questions.fact: The sclera is tough and helps protect the eye.

questions.q: What is the part of the eye that focuses light onto the retina?
questions.fact: As people get older, the lens gets stiffer, so many need reading glasses.

questions.q: What is a cataract?
choices: A big waterfall in the eye
A cloudy lens in the eye
questions.fact: Cataracts can be fixed by replacing the lens with an artificial one.

questions.q: What do eyelashes do?
choices: Keep dust and dirt out of your eyes
questions.fact: Eyelashes fall out and grow back every few months.

questions.q: What are eyebrows good for?
choices: Keeping sweat and rain out of your eyes
questions.fact: Eyebrows also help show feelings like surprise or anger.

questions.q: What is your nose's sense of smell called?
questions.fact: The smell sensors are in a small patch high inside your nose.

questions.q: What do the tiny hairs inside your nose do?
questions.fact: Mucus also traps dirt so it does not reach your lungs.

questions.q: What is the outer part of your ear that you can see called?
questions.fact: The pinna is shaped to funnel sound into your ear canal.

questions.q: What is the sense of taste called in science?
questions.fact: Your taste buds are mostly on the tiny bumps on your tongue, called papillae.

questions.q: What kind of doctor takes care of children?
questions.fact: Pediatric comes from a Greek word for child.

questions.q: What kind of doctor specializes in the heart?
questions.fact: Cardio comes from the Greek word for heart.

questions.q: What kind of doctor specializes in skin?
questions.fact: Dermatologists help with rashes, acne and checking moles.

questions.q: What kind of doctor specializes in the brain and nerves?
questions.fact: Neuro comes from the Greek word for nerve.

questions.q: What kind of dentist straightens teeth with braces?
questions.fact: Ortho means straight in Greek.

questions.q: What kind of doctor specializes in feet?
questions.fact: Pod comes from the Greek word for foot.

questions.q: What machine uses strong magnets to take detailed pictures inside the body?
questions.fact: MRI stands for magnetic resonance imaging.

questions.q: What do doctors use to look inside your ears?
questions.fact: Oto comes from the Greek word for ear.

questions.q: What is a cast used for?
choices: Holding a broken bone still while it heals
questions.fact: Broken bones in kids often heal in about four to eight weeks.

questions.q: Which ancient Greek doctor is called the father of medicine?
questions.fact: Many new doctors still take an oath named after him.

questions.q: Who is known as the founder of modern nursing?
questions.fact: She was called the Lady with the Lamp because she checked on soldiers at night.

questions.q: In what year did the first successful human heart transplant happen?
questions.fact: Surgeon Christiaan Barnard performed it in South Africa.

questions.q: What do we call a doctor who performs operations?
questions.fact: Surgeons wear masks and gloves to keep germs out of the patient's body.

questions.q: What is an X-ray mostly used to look at?
questions.fact: Bones block X-rays and show up white on the picture.

questions.q: What do you call medicine that kills bacteria?
questions.fact: Taking the whole course of antibiotics, as a doctor says, helps stop bacteria from coming back.

questions.q: What is first aid?
choices: Basic care given right away to someone hurt or sick
The first patient of the day
questions.fact: Knowing simple first aid can help in an emergency before help arrives.

questions.q: What should you do first for a small cut?
questions.fact: Then cover it with a clean bandage.

questions.q: What should you do for a minor burn?
choices: Put ice directly on it for an hour
Cool it under cool running water
questions.fact: Butter and ice can actually make burns worse.

questions.q: What should you do if someone is choking and cannot breathe or talk?
choices: Get help and give abdominal thrusts if trained
Make them lie down and sleep
questions.fact: Abdominal thrusts are also called the Heimlich maneuver.

questions.q: What number do you call for emergencies in the United States?
questions.fact: In the United Kingdom it is 999, and in much of Europe it is 112.

questions.q: What is CPR used for?
choices: Helping someone whose heart has stopped
questions.fact: CPR stands for cardiopulmonary resuscitation.

questions.q: What is a nosebleed?
choices: A sign of a cold only
Bleeding from tiny blood vessels inside the nose
questions.fact: Lean forward and pinch the soft part of your nose to stop a nosebleed.

questions.q: What is a concussion?
choices: A brain injury from a hit to the head
questions.fact: Wearing a helmet for biking and skating helps protect your brain.

questions.q: Why should you wear a helmet when biking?
choices: To protect your brain if you fall
questions.fact: Helmets greatly lower the chance of serious head injury in a crash.

questions.q: Why should you not look at screens right before bed?
choices: Bright light can make it harder to fall asleep
Screens make your eyes change color
It makes you grow slower overnight
questions.fact: Blue-rich light from screens can lower melatonin, the sleep hormone.

questions.q: What is the voice box's pair of folds that vibrate to make sound?
questions.fact: Vocal cords get longer and thicker during the teen years, which deepens voices.

questions.q: Why does your voice sound different on a recording?
choices: Your ears are blocked when you talk
You usually hear your voice through your bones too
questions.fact: Sound traveling through your skull makes your voice seem deeper to you.

questions.q: What part of the body makes up your Adam's apple?
questions.fact: Everyone has one, but it often sticks out more after puberty.

questions.q: What is the fastest-healing part of the body?
questions.fact: Mouth cuts often heal in just a few days.

questions.q: What is the strongest bone in the body?
questions.fact: The femur can support about 30 times the weight of your body.

questions.q: What percentage of your body weight is your skeleton, roughly?
questions.fact: Bones are light for how strong they are, because they are partly hollow and full of marrow.

questions.q: How many senses do people usually say we have?
questions.fact: Scientists say there are actually many more, like balance and temperature.

questions.q: What are the five classic senses?
choices: Sight, hearing, smell, taste and touch
Sight, sound, sleep, speech and smile
Hearing, walking, eating, seeing and talking
Taste, color, music, smell and heat
questions.fact: Each sense sends signals to a different part of the brain.

questions.q: What part of the brain handles vision?
choices: The frontal lobe at the front
The occipital lobe at the back
questions.fact: That is why a hard hit to the back of the head can make you see stars.

questions.q: What part of the brain helps with planning and decision-making?
questions.fact: The frontal lobe keeps developing until people are in their twenties.

questions.q: What is the space between the two halves of the brain connected by?
questions.fact: This thick band of nerves lets the left and right halves share information.

questions.q: What is short-term memory?
choices: Holding information for a short time, like a phone number
questions.fact: Most people can hold about seven things in short-term memory at once.

questions.q: What is muscle memory?
choices: Getting better at movements through practice
questions.fact: Practice builds brain pathways that make movements like riding a bike automatic.

questions.q: Which hand do about 90 percent of people prefer to write with?
questions.fact: About 1 in 10 people is left-handed.

questions.q: What is it called when someone can use both hands equally well?
questions.fact: True ambidexterity is quite rare.

questions.q: What is double-jointed really?
choices: Having two joints in one place
questions.fact: Doctors call it hypermobility.

questions.q: What is the dimple in your upper lip under your nose called?
questions.fact: Everyone has a philtrum, and scientists are still not sure if it has a purpose.

questions.q: What is the wall that divides the two nostrils called?
questions.fact: The septum is made of cartilage and bone.

questions.q: What is the belly button's medical name?
questions.fact: It marks where the umbilical cord was attached before you were born.

questions.q: What are the colored rings or patterns in your iris unique like?
questions.fact: Some security systems scan people's irises to identify them.

questions.q: What determines your eye color?
choices: How much melanin is in your iris
questions.fact: Brown is the most common eye color in the world.

questions.q: What is the most common eye color in the world?
questions.fact: Green is one of the rarest eye colors.

questions.q: Why do many babies' eyes change color in their first year?
choices: Melanin builds up in the iris over time
questions.fact: Many babies born with blue eyes end up with brown or green eyes.

questions.q: What is a mole on the skin?
choices: A small animal under the skin
A small cluster of pigment cells
questions.fact: It is good to show a doctor any mole that changes shape, size or color.

questions.q: What is acne?
questions.fact: Acne is very common during the teen years.

questions.q: What is dandruff?
choices: Flakes of dead skin from the scalp
questions.fact: Dandruff is not caused by being dirty.

questions.q: What are head lice?
choices: Tiny insects that live in hair and feed on blood from the scalp
questions.fact: Lice cannot fly or jump, they crawl from head to head.

questions.q: What is athlete's foot?
choices: A sports injury to the ankle
A fungus infection of the skin on the feet
questions.fact: Keeping feet dry and changing socks helps prevent it.

questions.q: What are warts caused by?
questions.fact: Touching a toad does not give you warts.

questions.q: What is asthma?
choices: A condition where the airways swell and narrow, making breathing hard
questions.fact: Many people with asthma use an inhaler to open their airways.

questions.q: What is diabetes?
choices: A condition where the body has trouble controlling blood sugar
questions.fact: Insulin helps sugar move from the blood into cells for energy.

questions.q: Which scientists first used insulin to treat diabetes in 1922?
questions.fact: Before insulin, type 1 diabetes was almost always deadly.

questions.q: What does a pacemaker do?
choices: Helps the heart keep a steady beat
questions.fact: A pacemaker is a small device placed under the skin.

questions.q: What is an organ donor?
choices: Someone who gives an organ to help another person
questions.fact: One donor can save several lives.

questions.q: What is the main job of the skin?
choices: Protecting the body from germs, sun and water loss
questions.fact: Skin also helps control body temperature through sweating.

questions.q: What part of the skin makes oil to keep it soft?
questions.fact: The scientific name is sebaceous glands.

questions.q: How often does your body replace the outer layer of skin?
questions.fact: New skin cells form deep in the epidermis and slowly move up to the surface.

questions.q: What do we call the tiny openings in the skin where sweat comes out?
questions.fact: You have millions of sweat pores over your body.

questions.q: What helps you grip things with your fingertips?
questions.fact: The ridges may also help you feel textures better.

questions.q: What does saliva contain that starts breaking down starch?
questions.fact: If you chew a cracker for a long time, it starts to taste sweeter because starch turns into sugar.

questions.q: About how big is an empty stomach?
choices: About the size of a pea
About the size of a fist
About the size of a basketball
About the size of a car
questions.fact: The stomach can stretch to hold about 1 to 1.5 liters of food.

questions.q: What is the ring of muscle that keeps stomach acid out of the esophagus?
questions.fact: When it does not close well, acid can rise and cause heartburn.

questions.q: What is heartburn?
choices: Stomach acid rising into the esophagus
Eating spicy food in the heart
questions.fact: Despite its name, heartburn has nothing to do with the heart.

questions.q: What does burping release?
choices: Swallowed air and gas from the stomach
questions.fact: Fizzy drinks make people burp because of the gas in them.

questions.q: Which body system includes lymph nodes and lymph vessels?
questions.fact: The lymphatic system carries fluid and helps fight infections.

questions.q: How many kidneys do most people have?
questions.fact: Kidneys sit near your back, just under your ribs.

questions.q: What are the tiny filtering units in your kidneys called?
questions.fact: Each kidney has about a million nephrons.

questions.q: Which organs help control the amount of water in your body?
questions.fact: When you drink a lot, your kidneys make more urine.

questions.q: Why do you need to go to the bathroom more when it is cold?
choices: Your body sends more fluid to the kidneys
questions.fact: When blood vessels in your skin tighten to save heat, more fluid goes to the kidneys.

questions.q: What is the growth spurt that happens to many kids as they become teenagers part of?
questions.fact: Growth plates near the ends of bones allow kids to grow taller.

questions.q: What are the areas near the ends of kids' long bones where growth happens called?
questions.fact: Growth plates close in the late teens, and then you stop getting taller.

questions.q: Are you taller in the morning or at night?
questions.fact: During the day, the cushions between your vertebrae get squeezed a little.

questions.q: What are the cushions between the bones of the spine called?
questions.fact: Discs act like shock absorbers when you walk, run and jump.

questions.q: What is it called when someone's spine curves sideways?
questions.fact: Doctors often check kids' backs for scoliosis because it can appear during growth spurts.

questions.q: What is arthritis?
choices: Pain and swelling in the joints
questions.fact: Arthritis is more common in older people, but kids can get it too.

questions.q: What are the two main tubes that branch from the windpipe into the lungs called?
questions.fact: They keep branching into smaller tubes like an upside-down tree.

questions.q: Why is smoking harmful to the lungs?
choices: It damages lung tissue and can cause diseases like cancer
It is only harmful to teeth
questions.fact: Lungs can slowly heal after someone stops smoking.

questions.q: Why do you breathe faster when you exercise?
questions.fact: Your heart beats faster too, to deliver the oxygen.

questions.q: What does the word cardio mean?
questions.fact: Cardio exercise, like running and swimming, makes your heart stronger.

questions.q: What sound does your heart make through a stethoscope?
questions.fact: The two sounds come from two sets of valves closing.

questions.q: How long does it take blood to travel around your whole body?
questions.fact: At rest, your heart pumps about 5 liters of blood a minute.

questions.q: What carries messages through your body in the nervous system?
questions.fact: Neurons pass signals using tiny pulses of electricity and chemicals.

questions.q: What is the gap between two nerve cells called?
questions.fact: Chemical messengers jump across the synapse to pass on a signal.

questions.q: What is the long tail of a nerve cell that carries signals away called?
questions.fact: Some axons are covered in a fatty layer that makes signals travel faster.

questions.q: What are the two main parts of the nervous system?
questions.fact: The central nervous system is the brain and spinal cord.

questions.q: What do pain signals help you do?
questions.fact: People who cannot feel pain often get hurt without noticing.

questions.q: What is the name of the thin tubes that carry tears from your eyes into your nose?
questions.fact: That is why your nose runs when you cry.

questions.q: What are the air-filled spaces in the bones around your nose called?
questions.fact: When sinuses get swollen during a cold, your face can feel stuffy and sore.

questions.q: What are the two lower chambers of the heart called?
questions.fact: The two upper chambers are called atria.

questions.q: What are the two upper chambers of the heart called?
questions.fact: Blood flows into the atria and then down into the ventricles.

questions.q: Which blood vessel brings blood from the body back into the heart?
questions.fact: The vena cava is the largest vein in the body.

questions.q: What are the arteries in your neck that carry blood to your brain called?
questions.fact: You can feel a pulse in your neck from the carotid arteries.

questions.q: What are the blood vessels that feed the heart muscle itself called?
questions.fact: When a coronary artery gets blocked, it can cause a heart attack.

questions.q: What is a heart attack?
choices: When the heart is broken by sadness
When the heart beats too slowly for fun
When the heart moves to the other side
When blood flow to part of the heart muscle is blocked
questions.fact: Calling emergency services right away is very important during a heart attack.

questions.q: About how much of your blood is made of red blood cells?
questions.fact: Doctors call this percentage the hematocrit.

questions.q: Which are the most common cells in your blood?
questions.fact: There are millions of red blood cells in a single tiny drop of blood.

questions.q: What shape is a red blood cell?
choices: A disc dented in the middle on both sides
questions.fact: This shape gives it lots of surface area to carry oxygen and lets it bend through tiny vessels.

questions.q: What do red blood cells lack that most other cells have?
questions.fact: Without a nucleus, there is more room to carry oxygen.

questions.q: What is it called when white blood cells eat germs?
questions.fact: Phagocytosis means cell eating.

questions.q: What is inflammation?
choices: Redness, heat and swelling as the body fights injury or germs
questions.fact: Inflammation is a sign that your immune system is at work.

questions.q: Why do cuts sometimes get swollen and red?
choices: Extra blood brings in immune cells to fight germs
questions.fact: If redness spreads or it gets very painful, a doctor should check it.

questions.q: What is pus?
choices: Dead white blood cells and germs from an infection
questions.fact: Pus is a sign that your body has been fighting bacteria.

questions.q: What does a vaccine usually contain?
choices: Live, dangerous germs at full strength
A harmless piece or weakened form of a germ
questions.fact: It lets your body practice fighting a germ safely.

questions.q: What is herd immunity?
choices: When you are immune to animals
When a group gets sick together
When enough people are immune that a disease cannot spread easily
questions.fact: It helps protect babies and people who cannot get certain vaccines.

questions.q: What do we call a disease that spreads from person to person?
questions.fact: Colds, flu and chickenpox are contagious diseases.

questions.q: What is a disease spreading around the whole world at once called?
questions.fact: The COVID-19 pandemic began in late 2019.

questions.q: What does a thermometer in a doctor's office measure?
questions.fact: Some thermometers measure temperature in the ear or on the forehead.

questions.q: Which joint is the largest in the human body?
questions.fact: The knee joins the femur, tibia and kneecap.

questions.q: Which joint in the body can move the most freely?
questions.fact: Because it moves so freely, the shoulder is also the joint that dislocates most often.

questions.q: What is a dislocation?
choices: When a bone pops out of its joint
questions.fact: A doctor can usually pop the bone back into place.

questions.q: What is the fluid in joints that keeps them moving smoothly?
questions.fact: It works like oil in a machine's hinges.

questions.q: What is the cracking sound when you crack your knuckles?
questions.fact: Studies have not found that knuckle cracking causes arthritis.

questions.q: Which part of the body contains about 22 bones fused or joined together?
questions.fact: Only one of these bones, the lower jaw, can move.

questions.q: What is the largest bone in the face?
questions.fact: The lower jaw, or mandible, is also the strongest bone in the face.

questions.q: What is the outer covering of a bone called?
questions.fact: The periosteum has nerves, which is why breaking a bone hurts so much.

questions.q: What is the spongy part inside the ends of long bones called?
questions.fact: Spongy bone is light but strong, like a honeycomb.

questions.q: What do we call bone tissue that is hard, dense and on the outside of bones?
questions.fact: Compact bone makes up most of the weight of your skeleton.

questions.q: Which vitamin and mineral together help build strong bones?
questions.fact: Weight-bearing exercise like running and jumping also helps make bones stronger.

questions.q: What happens to your bones when you jump and run often?
questions.fact: Bones respond to stress by adding more bone tissue.

questions.q: Which muscle lets you close your eyelids?
questions.fact: This ring-shaped muscle surrounds each eye.

questions.q: Which is the longest muscle in the human body?
questions.fact: The sartorius runs across the front of the thigh from the hip to the knee.

questions.q: Which is the smallest muscle in the human body?
questions.fact: The stapedius is in the middle ear and is only about 1 millimeter long.

questions.q: What is the tongue made of?
questions.fact: The tongue's muscles let it change shape for talking, eating and swallowing.

questions.q: What is unique about each person's tongue?
choices: It can taste only one flavor
Its print is unique, like a fingerprint
questions.fact: Scientists have studied tongue prints as a way to identify people.

questions.q: What happens to the pupils of your eyes in a dark room?
questions.fact: Bigger pupils let in more light so you can see better in the dark.

questions.q: How long does it take your eyes to fully adjust to the dark?
questions.fact: That is why astronomers avoid bright lights before stargazing.

questions.q: Why do some people need glasses to read as they get older?
choices: The lens of the eye gets stiffer
questions.fact: This condition is called presbyopia.

questions.q: What is the medical name for being nearsighted?
questions.fact: Spending time outdoors in daylight may help lower kids' chances of becoming nearsighted.

questions.q: What is the name for a blurry vision problem caused by an unevenly curved cornea?
questions.fact: Glasses or contact lenses can correct astigmatism.

questions.q: What is the special alphabet of raised dots that lets blind people read by touch?
questions.fact: Louis Braille invented it in the 1820s when he was a teenager.

questions.q: What is the language that uses hand shapes and movements, used by many deaf people?
questions.fact: There are many sign languages around the world, like American Sign Language and British Sign Language.

questions.q: What device helps some people with hearing loss hear better?
questions.fact: A cochlear implant is another device that can help people who are deeply deaf.

questions.q: What happens to your hearing if you listen to very loud music for a long time?
questions.fact: Keeping headphone volume at a moderate level helps protect your hearing.

questions.q: What is the name of the clear jelly that fills most of the eyeball?
questions.fact: Tiny clumps in this jelly cast shadows on the retina that look like floating specks, called floaters.

questions.q: What do you call the small, round muscle at the bottom of the stomach that lets food into the small intestine?
questions.fact: It opens a little at a time so food moves out of the stomach slowly.

questions.q: What is the main job of the large blood vessel called the pulmonary artery?
choices: Carrying blood from the heart to the lungs
questions.fact: Unlike most arteries, it carries blood that is low in oxygen.

questions.q: What is the body's natural painkiller chemical, released during exercise?
questions.fact: Endorphins can give people a happy feeling after a good workout.

questions.q: Which chemical messenger helps you feel happy and calm and is made mostly in your gut?
questions.fact: Most of the body's serotonin is actually made in the digestive system.

questions.q: What is the stress hormone your body makes when you are under pressure?
questions.fact: Short bursts of cortisol help you focus, but too much stress for too long is not healthy.

questions.q: What are the three main layers of the Earth?
questions.fact: The core is split into a liquid outer core and a solid inner core.

questions.q: Which layer of the Earth is the thickest?
questions.fact: The mantle is about 2,900 kilometers thick.

questions.q: Is Earth's outer core solid or liquid?
questions.fact: The swirling liquid iron in the outer core creates Earth's magnetic field.

questions.q: About how hot is Earth's inner core?
questions.fact: That is roughly as hot as the surface of the Sun.

questions.q: Why is Earth's inner core solid even though it is so hot?
choices: The huge pressure squeezes it solid
questions.fact: The pressure at the center of Earth is millions of times the air pressure at the surface.

questions.q: About how deep is the deepest hole people have ever drilled into Earth?
questions.fact: The Kola Superdeep Borehole in Russia reached about 12.2 kilometers, still only in the crust.

questions.q: How thick is Earth's crust under the oceans compared with under the continents?
choices: There is no crust under oceans
questions.fact: Ocean crust is often about 7 kilometers thick, while continental crust is usually 30 to 50 kilometers.

questions.q: What is the name for molten rock that comes out onto Earth's surface?
questions.fact: Lava can be hotter than 1,000 degrees Celsius.

questions.q: Which type of rock forms from layers of sand, mud or shells pressed together?
questions.fact: Most fossils are found in sedimentary rock.

questions.q: Which type of rock forms when other rocks are changed by heat and pressure?
questions.fact: Marble is metamorphic rock that started out as limestone.

questions.q: What is the slow cycle of rocks changing from one type to another called?
questions.fact: The rock cycle can take millions of years to complete.

questions.q: Which rock is so light and full of air bubbles that it can float on water?
questions.fact: Pumice forms when bubbly lava cools very quickly.

questions.q: Which shiny black volcanic glass forms when lava cools very fast?
questions.fact: Ancient people chipped obsidian into very sharp knives and arrowheads.

questions.q: Which speckled igneous rock is often used for kitchen countertops?
questions.fact: Granite forms when magma cools slowly deep underground.

questions.q: Which metamorphic rock is often used for statues, like Michelangelo's David?
questions.fact: Michelangelo carved David from a single block of marble from Carrara, Italy.

questions.q: Which rock splits into thin flat sheets and was used for chalkboards and roofs?
questions.fact: Slate forms from mudstone squeezed by heat and pressure.

questions.q: Which soft white sedimentary rock is made from tiny sea creature shells?
questions.fact: The White Cliffs of Dover in England are made of chalk.

questions.q: Which dark volcanic rock makes up most of the ocean floor?
questions.fact: Hawaii's islands are built mostly from basalt lava.

questions.q: What is the softest mineral on the Mohs hardness scale?
questions.fact: Talc is so soft you can scratch it with your fingernail.

questions.q: How many steps are on the Mohs scale of mineral hardness?
questions.fact: Diamond is a 10 and talc is a 1.

questions.q: Which common mineral makes up most beach sand?
questions.fact: Quartz is hard and does not wear away easily, so it lasts as sand.

questions.q: Which mineral is known as fool's gold because it looks like gold?
questions.fact: Pyrite is harder than gold and makes sparks when struck against steel.

questions.q: What do you call a hollow rock lined with crystals inside?
questions.fact: Geodes often look plain and round on the outside.

questions.q: What is the name for natural solid substances with a crystal structure, like quartz and salt?
questions.fact: Rocks are made of one or more minerals.

questions.q: What are the icicle-like rock formations that hang from cave ceilings called?
questions.fact: Stalactites hold tight to the ceiling, and stalagmites might grow up from the ground.

questions.q: What are the rock formations that grow up from cave floors called?
questions.fact: When a stalactite and stalagmite meet, they form a column.

questions.q: What mainly carves out most caves in limestone?
questions.fact: Rainwater picks up carbon dioxide, which makes a weak acid that slowly dissolves limestone.

questions.q: What is the longest known cave system in the world?
questions.fact: As of 2025, more than 680 kilometers of Mammoth Cave in Kentucky have been mapped.

questions.q: Which cave in Vietnam has the largest known cave passage, with its own jungle inside?
questions.fact: Son Doong is big enough to fit a whole city block of skyscrapers.

questions.q: What is a hole in the ground that suddenly forms when underground rock dissolves and collapses?
questions.fact: Florida has many sinkholes because of the limestone under the ground.

questions.q: What is the process of rock being broken down by wind, water and ice called?
questions.fact: Weathering breaks rock, and erosion carries the pieces away.

questions.q: What is the moving away of rocks and soil by wind, water or ice called?
questions.fact: The Grand Canyon was carved by erosion from the Colorado River.

questions.q: What is it called when rivers drop sand and mud in a new place?
questions.fact: River deltas form through deposition where rivers meet the sea.

questions.q: What is a wide, flat-topped hill with steep sides, common in the American Southwest?
questions.fact: Mesa means table in Spanish.

questions.q: What is a deep valley with steep sides, often carved by a river?
questions.fact: Canyons can take millions of years to form.

questions.q: What shape of valley do glaciers usually carve?
questions.fact: Rivers usually carve V-shaped valleys.

questions.q: What is a hill of sand piled up by the wind called?
questions.fact: Some sand dunes in the Sahara are over 150 meters tall.

questions.q: What is an area with plenty of water in a desert, where plants grow, called?
questions.fact: Oases often form where underground water comes up to the surface.

questions.q: What is a mirage?
choices: A trick of light that looks like water far away
questions.fact: Mirages happen when hot air near the ground bends light.

questions.q: What is the boundary where two tectonic plates move apart called?
questions.fact: The Mid-Atlantic Ridge is a divergent boundary under the ocean.

questions.q: What is the boundary where two tectonic plates push together called?
questions.fact: The Himalayas formed where the Indian plate pushes into the Eurasian plate.

questions.q: Which famous fault in California is where two plates slide past each other?
questions.fact: The San Andreas Fault runs about 1,200 kilometers through California.

questions.q: About how fast do tectonic plates move?
choices: About as fast as fingernails grow
questions.fact: Most plates move between about 2 and 10 centimeters a year.

questions.q: Which mountain range is still growing taller because two plates are pushing together?
questions.fact: Mount Everest rises a few millimeters every year.

questions.q: Who proposed the idea of continental drift in 1912?
questions.fact: Wegener noticed that the coasts of South America and Africa fit together like puzzle pieces.

questions.q: What is the point on Earth's surface right above where an earthquake starts called?
questions.fact: The point underground where the earthquake actually starts is called the focus or hypocenter.

questions.q: Which scale is used to measure an earthquake's magnitude today?
questions.fact: Each step up on the scale means about 32 times more energy released.

questions.q: What was the most powerful earthquake ever recorded?
questions.fact: The 1960 Valdivia earthquake had a magnitude of about 9.5.

questions.q: What are the smaller earthquakes that come after a big one called?
questions.fact: Aftershocks can keep happening for weeks or even years.

questions.q: What is a giant ocean wave caused by an undersea earthquake called?
questions.fact: Tsunami is a Japanese word meaning harbor wave.

questions.q: What should you do indoors during an earthquake?
questions.fact: Getting under a sturdy table protects you from falling objects.

questions.q: What is a warning sign of a tsunami at the beach?
choices: The sea suddenly pulls far back from the shore
questions.fact: If the water suddenly drains away, people should move to high ground right away.

questions.q: What is the opening in Earth's crust where lava and gas come out called?
questions.fact: The word volcano comes from Vulcan, the Roman god of fire.

questions.q: What is the bowl-shaped hole at the top of a volcano called?
questions.fact: A very large crater formed when a volcano collapses is called a caldera.

questions.q: What is the large bowl formed when a volcano collapses after a huge eruption?
questions.fact: Crater Lake in Oregon fills a caldera made about 7,700 years ago.

questions.q: What do we call a volcano that has not erupted in a very long time and is not expected to erupt again?
questions.fact: A dormant volcano is only sleeping and could erupt again.

questions.q: What kind of broad, gently sloping volcano is Mauna Loa in Hawaii?
questions.fact: Shield volcanoes get their name because they look like a warrior's shield lying on the ground.

questions.q: Which volcano in Italy buried the city of Pompeii?
questions.fact: Vesuvius is still an active volcano near the city of Naples.
