questions.q: Which astronaut recorded a music video of the song Space Oddity on the International Space Station in 2013?
questions.fact: It was the first music video filmed in space.

questions.q: Which astronaut spent almost a year on the International Space Station while an identical twin stayed on Earth for a NASA study?
questions.fact: The study compared the twins to learn how long spaceflight changes the human body.

questions.q: Who holds the record for the longest single trip in space, as of 2025?
questions.fact: Valeri Polyakov spent about 437 days in a row on the Mir space station in the 1990s.

questions.q: Which American astronaut has spent the most total days in space, as of 2025?
questions.fact: As of 2025, Peggy Whitson has spent close to 700 days in space over several missions.

questions.q: Who wrote and hosted the famous 1980 TV series Cosmos?
questions.fact: Carl Sagan also helped choose what went on the Voyager golden records.

questions.q: Which scientist studied black holes and wrote the book A Brief History of Time?
questions.fact: Stephen Hawking predicted that black holes slowly give off a faint glow, now called Hawking radiation.

questions.q: Who is the Hubble Space Telescope named after?
questions.fact: Edwin Hubble proved that many fuzzy patches in the sky are whole other galaxies.

questions.q: What problem did the Hubble Space Telescope have right after launch?
choices: Its main mirror was slightly the wrong shape
It was in the wrong orbit
questions.fact: Astronauts fixed it in 1993 by adding corrective optics, like giving Hubble glasses.

questions.q: How many times did astronauts fly to the Hubble Space Telescope to fix and upgrade it?
questions.fact: The last servicing mission was in 2009.

questions.q: What did Hubble's famous Pillars of Creation picture show?
choices: Towers of gas and dust where stars are forming
questions.fact: The pillars are in the Eagle Nebula, about 6,500 light-years away.

questions.q: What did the Hubble Deep Field picture reveal in a tiny dark patch of sky?
questions.fact: Almost every speck of light in the picture is a whole galaxy, not a single star.

questions.q: Which NASA space telescope studies X-rays from very hot things like exploding stars?
questions.fact: X-rays from space are blocked by Earth's air, so X-ray telescopes must be in orbit.

questions.q: Which giant radio telescope in Puerto Rico collapsed in 2020?
questions.fact: Arecibo appeared in movies, including the James Bond film GoldenEye.

questions.q: Which country built FAST, the giant 500-meter-wide radio telescope?
questions.fact: FAST sits in a natural bowl-shaped valley.

questions.q: What do radio telescopes detect?
questions.fact: Radio telescopes can work during the day and even through clouds.

questions.q: Why are many big telescopes built on tall mountains?
choices: It is cheaper to build there
There is less air and cloud to blur the view
questions.fact: Many of the world's best telescopes sit high on mountains in Hawaii and Chile.

questions.q: What is a galaxy?
choices: A huge group of stars, gas and dust held together by gravity
questions.fact: Scientists estimate there are hundreds of billions of galaxies in the universe we can observe.

questions.q: About how many stars are in the Milky Way?
questions.fact: Most of these stars are too faint to see without a telescope.

questions.q: Which type of galaxy looks like a round or oval ball of stars?
questions.fact: Elliptical galaxies usually have older stars and little gas for making new ones.

questions.q: What are the two small galaxies, seen from the Southern Hemisphere, that are close neighbors of the Milky Way?
questions.fact: They are named after explorer Ferdinand Magellan, whose crew described them.

questions.q: What is dark matter?
choices: Unseen matter that scientists detect only by its gravity
questions.fact: Scientists think there is about five times more dark matter than regular matter.

questions.q: What is a quasar?
choices: The super bright center of a faraway galaxy powered by a black hole
questions.fact: Some quasars shine brighter than a trillion Suns.

questions.q: What is a white dwarf?
choices: The small, hot leftover core of a star like the Sun
questions.fact: A white dwarf is about the size of Earth but has about as much mass as the Sun.

questions.q: What is a brown dwarf?
choices: An object too big to be a planet but too small to be a true star
questions.fact: Brown dwarfs never got hot enough to fuse hydrogen like real stars.

questions.q: What is a neutron star?
choices: The super-dense core left behind after some supernovas
questions.fact: A teaspoon of neutron star material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.

questions.q: What makes stars seem to twinkle?
questions.fact: Seen from space, stars do not twinkle at all.

questions.q: What happens to the light from a galaxy that is moving away from us?
questions.fact: This is called redshift, and it helps scientists measure how fast galaxies are moving.

questions.q: What is the faint glow left over from the Big Bang called?
questions.fact: It was discovered by accident in 1965 by two scientists who first thought the signal came from pigeon droppings on their antenna.

questions.q: What did the LIGO detectors observe for the first time in 2015?
questions.fact: The waves came from two black holes crashing together more than a billion light-years away.

questions.q: About how cold is deep space, far from any star?
questions.fact: That is only a few degrees above absolute zero, the coldest temperature possible.

questions.q: Which planet is fifth from the Sun?
questions.fact: Between Mars and Jupiter lies the asteroid belt.

questions.q: Which planet lies between Saturn and Neptune?
questions.fact: Uranus is the seventh planet from the Sun.

questions.q: Which is the largest of the four rocky planets?
questions.fact: The rocky planets are Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars.

questions.q: What kind of planets are Jupiter and Saturn?
questions.fact: They are made mostly of hydrogen and helium, like the Sun.

questions.q: What are Uranus and Neptune often called?
questions.fact: They contain lots of water, ammonia and methane, which scientists call ices.

questions.q: What would happen if a spacecraft tried to land on Jupiter?
choices: There is no solid surface to land on
questions.fact: The gas just gets thicker and hotter the deeper you go, until it would crush any spacecraft.

questions.q: About how many times wider is Jupiter than Earth?
questions.fact: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined.

questions.q: What is the main gas in Jupiter's atmosphere?
questions.fact: Jupiter is about 90 percent hydrogen by number of molecules.

questions.q: What has been happening to Jupiter's Great Red Spot over the last hundred years?
choices: It moved to the north pole
questions.fact: Even though it has shrunk, the Great Red Spot is still wider than Earth.

questions.q: What was the Great Dark Spot seen by Voyager 2 in 1989?
questions.fact: When Hubble looked at Neptune a few years later, the spot had disappeared.

questions.q: Many of the moons of Uranus are named after characters from which writer's plays?
questions.fact: Uranus has moons named Miranda, Titania, Oberon and Juliet.

questions.q: Which planet is named after the Roman god of war?
questions.fact: Mars's red color reminded ancient people of blood and battle.

questions.q: Which planet is named after the fast messenger of the Roman gods?
questions.fact: The name fits, because Mercury is the fastest-moving planet.

questions.q: Which planet is named after the Roman goddess of love and beauty?
questions.fact: Venus is the only planet named after a female god.

questions.q: Which planet is named after the king of the Roman gods?
questions.fact: It is a good name for the biggest planet in the solar system.

questions.q: Which planet is named after the Roman god of the sea?
questions.fact: Its deep blue color makes the name fit well.

questions.q: Which planet is named after an ancient Greek god of the sky?
questions.fact: Uranus is the only planet named after a Greek god instead of a Roman one.

questions.q: Which planet is named after the Roman god of farming?
questions.fact: Saturday is also named after Saturn.

questions.q: Which is the widest dwarf planet?
questions.fact: Eris is a little smaller than Pluto but has a bit more mass.

questions.q: How many dwarf planets are officially recognized, as of 2025?
questions.fact: As of 2025, they are Ceres, Pluto, Eris, Haumea and Makemake.

questions.q: Which dwarf planet is stretched into an egg shape because it spins so fast?
questions.fact: Haumea spins once about every four hours, one of the fastest spins of any big object in the solar system.

questions.q: Which NASA spacecraft visited both the asteroid Vesta and the dwarf planet Ceres?
questions.fact: Dawn was the first spacecraft to orbit two different worlds beyond Earth.

questions.q: Which NASA mission brought back a sample from the asteroid Bennu in 2023?
questions.fact: The sample capsule parachuted down into the Utah desert.

questions.q: What did NASA's DART spacecraft do in 2022?
choices: Crashed into an asteroid to change its path
questions.fact: DART hit the small asteroid Dimorphos and successfully shortened its orbit.

questions.q: Which Japanese spacecraft brought back samples from the asteroid Ryugu?
questions.fact: Hayabusa means peregrine falcon in Japanese.

questions.q: Which asteroid will pass very close to Earth, even closer than some satellites, in April 2029?
questions.fact: Scientists have checked carefully, and Apophis will not hit Earth in 2029.

questions.q: What flattened about 80 million trees in Siberia in 1908?
choices: A space rock exploding in the air
questions.fact: This is called the Tunguska event, and the blast happened above the ground.

questions.q: In which country did a meteor explode over the city of Chelyabinsk in 2013?
questions.fact: The blast shattered windows across the city, and many people caught it on dashboard cameras.

questions.q: In which country is the Hoba meteorite, the largest single meteorite ever found?
questions.fact: The Hoba meteorite weighs about 60 tons and was never moved from where it landed.

questions.q: In which US state is the famous Meteor Crater?
questions.fact: Meteor Crater is about 1.2 kilometers wide and was made about 50,000 years ago.

questions.q: Why do scientists search for meteorites in Antarctica?
choices: It is warmer than other places
Dark rocks are easy to spot on the white ice
questions.fact: Moving ice also carries meteorites to certain spots, piling them up.

questions.q: Have meteorites from Mars been found on Earth?
choices: Yes, they were blasted off Mars by impacts
questions.fact: Scientists can tell they are from Mars because gas trapped inside matches the Martian air.

questions.q: Which comet was easy to see without a telescope for months in 1997?
questions.fact: Hale-Bopp was visible to the naked eye for about 18 months.

questions.q: Which comet broke into pieces and crashed into Jupiter in 1994?
questions.fact: Some of the impact scars on Jupiter were bigger than Earth.

questions.q: What are space junk and space debris?
choices: Old satellites and broken pieces orbiting Earth
questions.fact: Even a tiny paint chip can be dangerous because it moves faster than a bullet.

questions.q: What is special about a satellite in geostationary orbit?
choices: It stays above the same spot on Earth
questions.fact: Geostationary satellites orbit about 36,000 kilometers above the equator.

questions.q: About how fast must something go to escape Earth's gravity completely?
questions.fact: This speed is called escape velocity.

questions.q: About how high above Earth does space begin, by the most common definition?
questions.fact: This boundary is called the Karman line.

questions.q: What is the floating, weightless feeling that astronauts have in orbit called?
questions.fact: In microgravity, astronauts can push off a wall with one finger and float across a room.

questions.q: Why do astronauts on the International Space Station exercise about two hours a day?
choices: To keep their bones and muscles strong
questions.fact: Without gravity to push against, bones and muscles get weaker quickly.

questions.q: What happens to astronauts' height while they live in space?
questions.fact: Without gravity squeezing their spines, astronauts can grow a few centimeters taller, but it goes away back on Earth.

questions.q: How do astronauts sleep on the International Space Station?
choices: In sleeping bags attached to the wall
questions.fact: In microgravity there is no up or down, so sleeping on a wall feels the same as on a floor.

questions.q: What do astronauts often eat instead of bread, so crumbs do not float into equipment?
questions.fact: Floating crumbs could get into astronauts' eyes or clog machines.

questions.q: What does the International Space Station recycle into clean drinking water?
questions.fact: The station's system recycles about 98 percent of the water on board.

questions.q: What shape does a candle flame take in microgravity?
questions.fact: Without gravity, hot air does not rise, so the flame spreads out evenly in all directions.

questions.q: Why are spacesuits usually white?
choices: To reflect sunlight and stay cooler
So they glow in the dark
questions.fact: In direct sunlight in space, a dark suit would soak up too much heat.

questions.q: What is a spacewalk officially called?
questions.fact: Astronauts on spacewalks are tied to the station with safety tethers.

questions.q: What keeps a spacecraft from burning up when it comes back into Earth's air?
questions.fact: Reentry heats the outside of a capsule to well over 1,000 degrees Celsius.

questions.q: What were the first animals sent into space, in 1947?
questions.fact: The fruit flies rode on a V-2 rocket and came back alive.

questions.q: What was the name of the first chimpanzee to fly into space, in 1961?
questions.fact: Ham was trained to pull levers during the flight, proving that tasks could be done in space.

questions.q: What were the dogs Belka and Strelka famous for in 1960?
choices: Pulling a sled to the South Pole
Being the first dogs to orbit Earth and come back alive
questions.fact: One of Strelka's puppies was given as a gift to US President John F. Kennedy's family.

questions.q: What is the 1990 photo of Earth taken by Voyager 1 from about 6 billion kilometers away called?
questions.fact: In it, Earth is a tiny speck less than a pixel wide.

questions.q: What is the famous 1972 photo of the whole Earth, taken by the Apollo 17 crew, called?
questions.fact: It is one of the most shared photographs ever taken.

questions.q: How do scientists find many planets around other stars?
choices: By watching for stars to dim slightly when a planet passes in front
questions.fact: This is called the transit method, and the Kepler telescope used it to find thousands of planets.

questions.q: What is the habitable zone around a star?
choices: The part of a planet with cities
The area where it is the right temperature for liquid water
questions.fact: It is also nicknamed the Goldilocks zone, not too hot and not too cold.

questions.q: Which star system, announced in 2017, has seven Earth-sized planets?
questions.fact: Three of TRAPPIST-1's planets are in the zone where liquid water might exist.

questions.q: What is the line between day and night on a planet or moon called?
questions.fact: Craters near the terminator cast long shadows, so it is the best place to look at the Moon with a telescope.

questions.q: What is the point in the sky directly above your head called?
questions.fact: The point directly below you, through the Earth, is called the nadir.

questions.q: How much is Earth's axis tilted?
questions.fact: This tilt is the reason Earth has seasons.

questions.q: What causes Earth's seasons?
questions.fact: When your half of Earth tilts toward the Sun, sunlight hits more directly and it is summer.

questions.q: During which month is Earth closest to the Sun?
questions.fact: Earth is closest to the Sun in early January, during winter in the Northern Hemisphere.

questions.q: What is the day with the most hours of daylight in the year called?
questions.fact: In the Northern Hemisphere, it usually falls on June 20 or 21.

questions.q: What is special about an equinox?
choices: Day and night are about the same length everywhere
questions.fact: Equinox comes from Latin words meaning equal night.

questions.q: On average, which planet is closest to Earth?
questions.fact: Venus comes closest at times, but Mercury stays nearer on average because it never strays far from the Sun.

questions.q: Can the Great Wall of China be seen with the naked eye from the Moon?
questions.fact: The wall is very long but narrow, and from the Moon even whole continents look small.

questions.q: Which space agency is called ESA?
questions.fact: ESA has more than 20 member countries.

questions.q: What is India's space agency called?
questions.fact: ISRO stands for Indian Space Research Organisation.

questions.q: What is Japan's space agency called?
questions.fact: JAXA stands for Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency.

questions.q: Which NASA center in Florida launches many rockets?
questions.fact: Apollo 11 launched from Kennedy Space Center in 1969.

questions.q: Which NASA center in Houston runs Mission Control for astronaut flights?
questions.fact: When astronauts radio Houston, they are talking to Mission Control there.

questions.q: What is the zone of orbits up to about 2,000 kilometers above Earth called?
questions.fact: Most satellites, and every human spaceflight except Apollo, have stayed in low Earth orbit.

questions.q: What was the name of the world's first space station, launched in 1971?
questions.fact: Salyut 1 was launched by the Soviet Union.

questions.q: Which moon will NASA's Dragonfly flying drone explore?
questions.fact: As of 2025, Dragonfly is planned to launch in 2028 and fly from place to place on Saturn's biggest moon.

questions.q: What is the European spacecraft launched in 2023 to study Jupiter's icy moons called?
questions.fact: JUICE stands for Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer.

questions.q: What is the science that studies how the whole universe began and changes called?
questions.fact: Cosmos comes from a Greek word for an orderly world or universe.

questions.q: What is a parsec?
questions.fact: Astronomers use parsecs to measure the distances to stars and galaxies.

questions.q: How long does a radio message take to travel between Earth and Mars?
questions.fact: That is why Mars rovers cannot be driven live with a joystick and must do many things on their own.

questions.q: What powers most satellites near Earth?
questions.fact: Sunlight in space is never blocked by clouds, so solar panels work very well there.

questions.q: What powers spacecraft that travel far from the Sun, like Voyager?
choices: Nuclear batteries using heat from plutonium
questions.fact: Far from the Sun, sunlight is too weak for solar panels to give enough power.

questions.q: Why do most rockets launch toward the east?
choices: To get a speed boost from Earth's spin
Because the wind blows that way
questions.fact: Earth spins toward the east at up to about 1,670 kilometers per hour at the equator.

questions.q: How many engines are on the first stage of a Falcon 9 rocket?
questions.fact: The rocket's name comes from its nine engines and the Millennium Falcon from Star Wars.

questions.q: About how far from Earth does the James Webb Space Telescope orbit?
questions.fact: That is about four times farther than the Moon.

questions.q: Which NASA spacecraft orbited Jupiter from 1995 to 2003?
questions.fact: Galileo also dropped a probe into Jupiter's atmosphere.

questions.q: What are Jupiter's Trojan asteroids?
choices: Asteroids that share Jupiter's path around the Sun
questions.fact: They travel in two big groups, one ahead of Jupiter and one behind it.

questions.q: NASA's Lucy mission to the Trojan asteroids is named after what?
choices: A famous fossil of an early human ancestor
questions.fact: The Lucy fossil got its name from the Beatles song Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds.

questions.q: What made most of the craters on the Moon?
questions.fact: With no air or weather, the Moon keeps its craters for billions of years.

questions.q: What did Galileo see on the Moon with his telescope in 1609 and 1610?
questions.fact: Before this, many people believed the Moon was a perfectly smooth ball.

questions.q: How many space agencies work together to run the International Space Station?
questions.fact: The partners are from the United States, Russia, Europe, Japan and Canada.

questions.q: What is the big robotic arm on the International Space Station, built by Canada, called?
questions.fact: Canadarm2 can move along the outside of the station and grab arriving spacecraft.

questions.q: Which country do tacos come from?
questions.fact: Tacos were eaten in Mexico long before the Spanish arrived, often filled with small fish.

questions.q: Kimchi, a spicy fermented cabbage dish, is a national food of which country?
questions.fact: Many Korean families make big batches of kimchi together in late autumn, a tradition called kimjang.

questions.q: Which country does the stir-fried noodle dish pad thai come from?
questions.fact: Pad thai became popular in Thailand in the 1930s and 1940s.

questions.q: Which country is famous for pho, a noodle soup with broth and herbs?
questions.fact: Pho is often eaten for breakfast in Vietnam.

questions.q: Which country is famous for fish and chips?
questions.fact: Fish and chips were so important in Britain that they were not rationed during World War II.

questions.q: Which country is famous for haggis, made with sheep's heart, liver and lungs?
questions.fact: Haggis is traditionally eaten on Burns Night, January 25.

questions.q: Poutine, fries topped with cheese curds and gravy, comes from which country?
questions.fact: Poutine was first served in the province of Quebec in the 1950s.

questions.q: Pierogi, filled dumplings, are a famous food of which country?
questions.fact: Pierogi can be filled with potato, cheese, cabbage, meat or even fruit.

questions.q: Goulash, a stew seasoned with paprika, comes from which country?
questions.fact: Goulash was first cooked by Hungarian cattle herders in big kettles over open fires.

questions.q: Moussaka, a baked dish of eggplant and meat, is famous in which country?
questions.fact: Greek moussaka is usually topped with a thick, creamy white sauce.

questions.q: Which crispy fried balls made from chickpeas or fava beans are popular across the Middle East?
questions.fact: Falafel is often stuffed inside pita bread with salad and tahini sauce.

questions.q: Which noodle soup is hugely popular in Japan but first came from China?
questions.fact: Japan has a museum all about ramen in Yokohama.

questions.q: What is the name of the small Chinese dishes, like dumplings and buns, often served with tea?
questions.fact: Dim sum is a big part of Cantonese food from southern China.

questions.q: Which famous roast duck dish is named after China's capital?
questions.fact: Peking is an old spelling of Beijing.

questions.q: What is the thin, dried seaweed used to wrap sushi rolls called?
questions.fact: Nori is made by pressing seaweed into thin sheets, a bit like making paper.

questions.q: What is most of the green "wasabi" served with sushi outside Japan actually made from?
questions.fact: Real wasabi is a rare plant that is hard to grow, so most restaurants use horseradish colored green.

questions.q: What is tempura?
choices: Food dipped in light batter and deep-fried
questions.fact: Portuguese traders and missionaries are thought to have brought the idea of tempura to Japan in the 1500s.

questions.q: What is miso made from?
questions.fact: Miso soup is eaten at many Japanese breakfasts.

questions.q: What are edamame?
questions.fact: Edamame are often boiled in their pods with salt and popped out to eat.

questions.q: Which Korean dish is a bowl of rice topped with vegetables, meat, an egg and chili paste, all mixed together?
questions.fact: Bibimbap means "mixed rice" in Korean.

questions.q: Which Peruvian dish is made of raw fish "cooked" in lime or lemon juice?
questions.fact: The acid in citrus juice changes the fish's proteins, a little like heat does.

questions.q: Which black bean and pork stew is a national dish of Brazil?
questions.fact: Feijoada is often served on Saturdays in Brazil with rice, greens and orange slices.

questions.q: Which corn cakes are a daily food in Venezuela and Colombia?
questions.fact: Arepas can be grilled, baked or fried and split open to hold fillings.

questions.q: Which fried dough sticks, often dipped in hot chocolate, are a classic treat in Spain?
questions.fact: In Spain, churros and chocolate are a popular breakfast.

questions.q: What is the name for small Spanish dishes shared as snacks or a meal?
questions.fact: Tapa means "lid" or "cover" in Spanish, and one story says bars covered drinks with a slice of bread.

questions.q: Which cold tomato soup comes from southern Spain?
questions.fact: Gazpacho is a refreshing summer soup from Andalusia.

questions.q: Which fermented cabbage dish is especially popular in Germany?
questions.fact: Sauerkraut means "sour cabbage" in German.

questions.q: Which country is famous for cheese fondue, where you dip bread into melted cheese?
questions.fact: Tradition says if you drop your bread in the fondue pot, you have to do a silly forfeit.

questions.q: Which long, thin French bread was added to UNESCO's list of cultural heritage in 2022?
questions.fact: French bakeries make billions of baguettes each year.

questions.q: What are thin French pancakes called?
questions.fact: Savory buckwheat crêpes from Brittany are often called galettes.

questions.q: What are escargots, a famous French dish?
questions.fact: Escargots are usually cooked with garlic, butter and parsley.

questions.q: Which vegetable stew from the south of France shares its name with a Pixar movie?
questions.fact: Ratatouille usually has eggplant, zucchini, peppers, tomatoes and onions.

questions.q: Which creamy Italian rice dish is stirred slowly while adding broth?
questions.fact: Risotto is made with short-grain rice like Arborio, which releases starch to make it creamy.

questions.q: What does the name of the Italian dessert tiramisu mean?
questions.fact: Tiramisu has coffee-soaked biscuits, which may be where the "pick me up" name comes from.

questions.q: Which green Italian sauce is made from basil, pine nuts, garlic, cheese and olive oil?
questions.fact: Pesto comes from Genoa, and its name comes from an Italian word for pounding.

questions.q: Traditional mozzarella di bufala is made from the milk of which animal?
questions.fact: Water buffalo milk has more fat than cow's milk, which makes the cheese very creamy.

questions.q: Which famous hard Italian cheese has the full name Parmigiano-Reggiano?
questions.fact: Wheels of Parmigiano-Reggiano weigh around 40 kilograms each.

questions.q: Pizza Margherita is said to be named after which person?
questions.fact: Its red tomato, white mozzarella and green basil match the colors of the Italian flag.

questions.q: Which salty white cheese, often made from sheep's milk, is famous in Greece?
questions.fact: Feta is stored in salty water called brine to keep it fresh.

questions.q: Which Greek dip is made from yogurt, cucumber and garlic?
questions.fact: Tzatziki is often served with grilled meat and pita bread.

questions.q: Which sweet pastry is made from layers of thin dough, chopped nuts and honey or syrup?
questions.fact: Baklava was a famous treat in the kitchens of the Ottoman sultans.

questions.q: What is the meat roasted on a tall turning spit and shaved off in thin slices for wraps called in the Middle East?
questions.fact: Similar dishes are called döner kebab in Turkey and gyros in Greece.

questions.q: Couscous, a staple of North Africa, is made from what?
questions.fact: Couscous is steamed rather than boiled in traditional North African cooking.

questions.q: What is the cone-shaped clay pot used to cook slow stews in Morocco called?
questions.fact: The cone shape lets steam rise, cool and drip back down to keep food moist.

questions.q: Which spicy tomato rice dish is a favorite across West Africa, with friendly rivalry between Ghana and Nigeria?
questions.fact: Fans in Ghana and Nigeria argue playfully about which country makes the best jollof.

questions.q: What spongy flatbread from Ethiopia is used as both a plate and a spoon?
questions.fact: Injera is made from teff, a tiny grain that grows in the Ethiopian highlands.

questions.q: Which dark, salty spread made from yeast extract is an Australian favorite?
questions.fact: Vegemite was created in 1922, and Australians usually spread it very thinly on toast.

questions.q: Which meringue dessert with fruit on top is claimed by both Australia and New Zealand?
questions.fact: It was named after the Russian ballerina Anna Pavlova.

questions.q: Which Indian rice dish is cooked in layers with spices and often meat?
questions.fact: Biryani is often flavored with saffron, which turns some of the rice golden.

questions.q: What is naan?
choices: A flatbread baked in a clay oven
questions.fact: Naan dough is slapped onto the hot inside wall of a clay oven called a tandoor.

questions.q: What is a samosa?
choices: A fried pastry filled with spiced potatoes or meat
questions.fact: Samosas are usually shaped like triangles.

questions.q: What are bagels boiled in water before?
questions.fact: Boiling gives bagels their shiny, chewy crust.

questions.q: Which German city is the frankfurter sausage named after?
questions.fact: Hot dogs in the United States grew out of the frankfurter.

questions.q: Buffalo wings were first made in which US city?
questions.fact: Buffalo wings are said to have been first served at the Anchor Bar in 1964.

questions.q: Which US city is famous for cheesesteak sandwiches?
questions.fact: A Philly cheesesteak has thin slices of beef with melted cheese on a long roll.

questions.q: Which US city is famous for deep-dish pizza?
questions.fact: Deep-dish pizza is baked in a tall pan, with the sauce often on top of the cheese.

questions.q: Which thick stew from Louisiana is often made with okra, shrimp and sausage?
questions.fact: Gumbo may come from a West African word for okra.

questions.q: Who invented nachos in 1943?
questions.fact: Nachos were named after their inventor, whose nickname was Nacho.

questions.q: In which country was the Caesar salad invented?
questions.fact: Restaurant owner Caesar Cardini is said to have created it in Tijuana in 1924.

questions.q: Who invented the chocolate chip cookie in the 1930s?
questions.fact: Ruth Wakefield ran the Toll House Inn in Massachusetts.

questions.q: Which US state has the most active volcanoes?
questions.fact: Alaska has more than 50 volcanoes that have erupted in recorded history.

questions.q: Which US state is known as the Bluegrass State?
questions.fact: Kentucky's famous horse race, the Kentucky Derby, has been held since 1875.

questions.q: Which city is nicknamed the City of Light?
questions.fact: Paris was one of the first big cities to light its streets with gas lamps.

questions.q: Which city is split between Europe and Asia?
questions.fact: Istanbul was called Byzantium and then Constantinople in the past.

questions.q: Which city is famous for its canals and gondolas?
questions.fact: Venice has no cars on its islands; people get around by boat or on foot.

questions.q: What is the great bell inside London's Elizabeth Tower called?
questions.fact: Many people call the whole clock tower Big Ben, but the name belongs to the bell.

questions.q: In which Italian city is the famous Leaning Tower?
questions.fact: The tower started to lean while it was still being built, because the ground beneath it is soft.

questions.q: Which city has the giant statue of Christ the Redeemer on a mountain?
questions.fact: The statue is about 30 meters tall and its arms stretch about 28 meters.

questions.q: In which city is the famous Opera House with roofs shaped like sails?
questions.fact: The Sydney Opera House roofs are covered with more than one million tiles.

questions.q: In which Indian city is the Taj Mahal?
questions.fact: The Taj Mahal seems to change color from pink to white to gold during the day.

questions.q: As of 2025, which city has the tallest building in the world?
questions.fact: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai is about 828 meters tall.

questions.q: In which city is the Kremlin?
questions.fact: Kremlin means "fortress inside a city" in Russian.

questions.q: In which country is Neuschwanstein, the castle that inspired Disney's Sleeping Beauty Castle?
questions.fact: King Ludwig II built Neuschwanstein in the 1800s but lived there only a few months.

questions.q: In which country is Stonehenge?
questions.fact: Stonehenge is on Salisbury Plain in the county of Wiltshire.

questions.q: In which city is the Sagrada Família church, still being built after more than 140 years?
questions.fact: Work on the Sagrada Família started in 1882, and the architect Antoni Gaudí spent decades on it.

questions.q: In which city is the Forbidden City palace?
questions.fact: Ordinary people were not allowed inside the Forbidden City for about 500 years.

questions.q: In which city is the Brandenburg Gate?
questions.fact: The Brandenburg Gate became a symbol of German unity after the Berlin Wall came down.

questions.q: In which country is Uluru, the giant red rock also called Ayers Rock?
questions.fact: Uluru is sacred to the local Aboriginal people, the Anangu.

questions.q: In which city is Hagia Sophia, a building that has been a church, a mosque and a museum?
questions.fact: Hagia Sophia was finished in AD 537, and its giant dome amazed people for centuries.

questions.q: In which Spanish city is the Alhambra palace?
questions.fact: The Alhambra was built by Moorish rulers and is covered in detailed tile and carved patterns.

questions.q: In which city is the Louvre, the museum that holds the Mona Lisa?
questions.fact: The Louvre is the most visited art museum in the world.

questions.q: In which country are the famous Pyramids of Giza?
questions.fact: Giza is right next to Egypt's capital, Cairo.

questions.q: In which country is the ancient city of Petra?
questions.fact: Petra was named one of the New Seven Wonders of the World in 2007.

questions.q: In which country is the Great Wall?
questions.fact: The Great Wall, with all its branches, is more than 20,000 kilometers long.

questions.q: In which Canadian city is the CN Tower?
questions.fact: The CN Tower has a glass floor where you can look straight down 342 meters.

questions.q: In which city do people climb the Spanish Steps and toss coins into the Trevi Fountain?
questions.fact: About 3,000 euros in coins are thrown into the Trevi Fountain each day, and the money goes to charity.

questions.q: In which city are the Petronas Twin Towers?
questions.fact: A sky bridge connects the two towers on their 41st and 42nd floors.

questions.q: What are the imaginary lines on a map that run from the North Pole to the South Pole called?
questions.fact: Lines of longitude are also called meridians.

questions.q: Through which place in London does the Prime Meridian pass?
questions.fact: Visitors to Greenwich can stand with one foot in each hemisphere.

questions.q: At what latitude is the Equator?
questions.fact: The North Pole is at 90 degrees north latitude.

questions.q: Which line of latitude lies about 23.5 degrees south of the Equator?
questions.fact: The Tropic of Capricorn passes through Australia, South America and southern Africa.

questions.q: Which line of latitude lies about 23.5 degrees north of the Equator?
questions.fact: The Tropic of Cancer passes through Mexico, Egypt, India and China.

questions.q: In which ocean is most of the International Date Line?
questions.fact: If you cross the International Date Line going west, you skip ahead one day.

questions.q: What is the box on a map that explains what its symbols mean called?
questions.fact: A map legend is also called a key.

questions.q: What is the drawing on a map that shows north, south, east and west called?
questions.fact: Old compass roses were often drawn with fancy points that looked like flower petals.

questions.q: What do contour lines on a map show?
questions.fact: When contour lines are close together, the land is steep.

questions.q: Which two hemispheres is Australia in?
questions.fact: Australia is entirely south of the Equator and east of the Prime Meridian.

questions.q: Which hemisphere are all 50 US states in, north or south?
questions.fact: All 50 US states, even Hawaii, are north of the Equator.

questions.q: What does a map projection do?
choices: Shows the round Earth on a flat surface
questions.fact: Every flat map stretches something, which is why Greenland looks huge on many maps.

questions.q: What type of map shows the height of mountains and valleys?
questions.fact: Hikers use topographic maps to plan routes and see how steep a trail will be.

questions.q: What is a map that shows borders between countries and states called?
questions.fact: Political maps usually color each country differently so they stand out.

questions.q: Which instrument has a magnetic needle that points north?
questions.fact: A compass points to magnetic north, which is not exactly the same spot as the North Pole.

questions.q: Which African country has the famous Serengeti plains, known for the great wildebeest migration?
questions.fact: More than a million wildebeest move across the Serengeti each year looking for fresh grass.

questions.q: Which European country is famous for windmills, tulips and wooden shoes?
questions.fact: About a quarter of the Netherlands is below sea level.

questions.q: In which country would you find the city of Kyoto with its many temples?
questions.fact: Kyoto was spared from bombing in World War II because of its cultural treasures.

questions.q: What do people call the high, flat grasslands of Argentina?
questions.fact: Cowboys called gauchos herd cattle on the Pampas.

questions.q: What are the huge grasslands of central Russia and Kazakhstan called?
questions.fact: Horse riders like the Mongols once crossed the steppes on their great journeys.

questions.q: What is the cold, treeless land of the far north called?
questions.fact: Under the tundra lies permafrost, ground that stays frozen all year.

questions.q: What is the huge northern forest of pine and spruce trees that circles the Arctic called?
questions.fact: The taiga is the largest land biome in the world.

questions.q: Which rainforest is the largest in the world?
questions.fact: The Amazon rainforest spreads across nine countries.

questions.q: Which country has most of the Amazon rainforest?
questions.fact: About 60 percent of the Amazon rainforest is in Brazil.

questions.q: Which region in the far north of Scandinavia is famous for reindeer herding by the Sámi people?
questions.fact: Finland's part of Lapland is often called the home of Santa Claus.

questions.q: Which region at the southern tip of South America is shared by Argentina and Chile?
questions.fact: Patagonia has glaciers, huge mountains and very strong winds.

questions.q: Which huge region of Russia east of the Ural Mountains is known for its freezing winters?
questions.fact: The village of Oymyakon in Siberia is one of the coldest places where people live year round.

questions.q: Which country has more time zones on its mainland than any other?
questions.fact: Russia stretches across 11 time zones.

questions.q: Even though China is very wide, how many official time zones does it use?
questions.fact: All of China uses Beijing time, so the sun can rise very late in the far west.

questions.q: What is the lowest point on land on Earth?
questions.fact: The shore of the Dead Sea is more than 400 meters below sea level.

questions.q: In which ocean is the Mariana Trench, the deepest part of the ocean?
questions.fact: The Mariana Trench is about 11,000 meters deep, deeper than Mount Everest is tall.

questions.q: Which mountain range has the 10 highest mountains in the world?
questions.fact: All mountains over 8,000 meters tall are in Asia.

questions.q: Which country has the most volcanoes that have erupted in recorded history?
questions.fact: Indonesia sits on the Ring of Fire, where many earthquakes and eruptions happen.

questions.q: What is the ring of volcanoes and earthquake zones around the Pacific Ocean called?
questions.fact: About three quarters of the world's active volcanoes are in the Ring of Fire.

questions.q: Which famous road in Germany has no general speed limit on many stretches?
questions.fact: Some parts of the Autobahn do have speed limits, especially near cities.

questions.q: Which famous avenue in Paris leads to the Arc de Triomphe?
questions.fact: The Tour de France bike race usually finishes on the Champs-Élysées.

questions.q: Which famous old highway in the United States ran from Chicago to Los Angeles?
questions.fact: Route 66 was nicknamed the Mother Road.

questions.q: Which country is known for having more sheep than people?
questions.fact: As of 2025, New Zealand has about four or five sheep for every person.

questions.q: Which European country is shaped a bit like a hexagon, so its people call it L'Hexagone?

questions.q: Which country is home to the city of Casablanca?
questions.fact: Casablanca means "white house" in Spanish.

questions.q: What is the name of the narrow strip of land that connects North and South America?
questions.fact: The Isthmus of Panama formed about 3 million years ago, joining the two continents.

questions.q: Which body of water lies between Australia and New Zealand?

questions.q: Which sea is home to Australia's Great Barrier Reef?
questions.fact: The Coral Sea is named after its huge coral reefs.

questions.q: Which sea in northern Europe is bordered by Sweden, Finland, Poland and Germany?

questions.q: Which bay in Canada is so big it is sometimes called an inland sea?

questions.q: Which bay in Canada has the highest tides in the world?

questions.q: Which bay between India and Myanmar is the largest bay in the world?

questions.q: Which country is Bora Bora part of?

questions.q: Which country owns the Canary Islands off the coast of Africa?

questions.q: Which country owns the Azores islands in the Atlantic?

questions.q: Which European country does the Faroe Islands belong to?

questions.q: Which US territory in the Caribbean has San Juan as its capital?

questions.q: Which US territory in the Pacific has the motto "Where America's Day Begins"?

questions.q: Which country has the largest Muslim population in the world?
questions.fact: As of 2025, Indonesia has more than 230 million Muslims.

questions.q: Which African river is the deepest river in the world?

questions.q: Which river flows through Baghdad?

questions.q: Which city in the Netherlands has more bicycles than people?

questions.q: Which country is often said to have the most islands in the world?
questions.fact: Sweden has more than 260,000 islands, though most are tiny and empty.

questions.q: Which is the largest country by area that lies completely inside Europe?
questions.fact: Russia is bigger, but most of Russia's land is in Asia.

questions.q: Which East African country did Winston Churchill call the Pearl of Africa?
questions.fact: Uganda is home to about half of the world's mountain gorillas.

questions.q: Which country's largest city is Johannesburg?
questions.fact: Johannesburg grew very fast after gold was discovered there in 1886.

questions.q: Which Indian city is home to the Bollywood film industry?
questions.fact: The name Bollywood mixes Bombay, Mumbai's old name, with Hollywood.

questions.q: Which mountain range stretches across Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia?
questions.fact: In Greek myths, the giant Atlas held up the sky, and the mountains were named after him.

questions.q: What is the highest mountain in the British Isles?

questions.q: What is the longest river in the United Kingdom?

questions.q: In which country is the Okavango Delta, a river delta that ends in the desert instead of the sea?

questions.q: In which country is the Yucatán Peninsula, home to many Maya ruins?

questions.q: Which peninsula do Spain and Portugal share?
questions.fact: The tiny British territory of Gibraltar is also on the Iberian Peninsula.

questions.q: Which three countries make up Scandinavia?
questions.fact: Finland and Iceland are often grouped with them as the Nordic countries.

questions.q: Which three countries are known together as the Benelux?

questions.q: What are people from the Netherlands called?

questions.q: Which European capital city sits on the Vltava River?

questions.q: Which famous hiking trail runs from Georgia to Maine?

questions.q: What is the capital of the German state of Bavaria?

questions.q: Which Australian city is the capital of the state of Victoria?

questions.q: Which country is home to the Black Forest, famous for cuckoo clocks and cake?

questions.q: Who became the first emperor of Rome?

questions.q: Which of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World is the only one still standing?
questions.fact: The Great Pyramid was built about 4,500 years ago for the pharaoh Khufu.

questions.q: What were the picture symbols used for writing in ancient Egypt called?

questions.q: Which young pharaoh's tomb was found almost untouched in 1922?
questions.fact: Howard Carter found King Tut's tomb in the Valley of the Kings, packed with golden treasures.

questions.q: What wedge-shaped writing was invented in ancient Mesopotamia?

questions.q: Which river did farming in ancient Egypt depend on?
questions.fact: The Nile flooded every year and left rich black soil behind for growing crops.

questions.q: Which Greek city-state was famous for its tough warriors?

questions.q: In which ancient Greek city did democracy first develop?

questions.q: Which Roman leader was killed on the Ides of March in 44 BC?

questions.q: What language did the ancient Romans speak?

questions.q: According to legend, which city was captured by soldiers hiding inside a wooden horse?

questions.q: Which Mongol leader founded the Mongol Empire in 1206?

questions.q: Which Italian traveler wrote about his journey to China in the 1200s?

questions.q: What was the famous network of trade routes between China and the Mediterranean called?

questions.q: During which Chinese dynasty was most of the Great Wall we see today built?

questions.q: Who was the first emperor of a united China?
questions.fact: The name China may come from Qin, which is said like "chin".

questions.q: What is the army of clay soldiers buried with China's first emperor called?

questions.q: Which Chinese thinker taught about respect, family and good behavior about 2,500 years ago?
questions.fact: The sayings of Confucius were collected by his students in a book called the Analects.

questions.q: Which ancient Chinese general is said to have written The Art of War?

questions.q: Which empire built Machu Picchu high in the Andes?

questions.q: Which civilization built the great pyramid city of Chichen Itza in Mexico?

questions.q: Which Spanish conquistador conquered the Inca Empire?

questions.q: What was the capital of the Inca Empire?

questions.q: What did the Inca use their knotted strings, called quipus, for?
questions.fact: The Inca had no written alphabet, so quipus helped them track numbers like taxes and harvests.

questions.q: Which seafaring raiders from Scandinavia attacked coasts across Europe from about 800 to 1050?

questions.q: Which Viking explorer reached North America around the year 1000?

questions.q: Which battle in 1066 led to the Norman conquest of England?

questions.q: Which long embroidered cloth tells the story of the Norman conquest of England?

questions.q: What was the deadly plague that swept across Europe in the 1300s called?

questions.q: What were the wars fought over the Holy Land between Christian and Muslim armies in the Middle Ages called?
questions.fact: The First Crusade began in 1096.

questions.q: Which French teenager led armies during the Hundred Years' War?

questions.q: How long did the Hundred Years' War between England and France actually last?

questions.q: What was the medieval system where lords gave land to people in return for loyalty and service?

questions.q: In the Middle Ages, what was a boy called when he first began training to become a knight?
questions.fact: Pages started training around age 7 and became squires at about 14.

questions.q: What was the time of rebirth in art and learning that began in Italy in the 1300s called?
questions.fact: Renaissance is a French word that means rebirth.

questions.q: Who painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?

questions.q: Who started the Protestant Reformation by writing his 95 Theses in 1517?
questions.fact: The new printing press helped Luther's ideas spread quickly across Europe.

questions.q: Which English king had six wives?

questions.q: Which queen ruled England when the Spanish Armada was defeated in 1588?
questions.fact: Elizabeth I ruled for 44 years and never married.

questions.q: Who wrote the play Romeo and Juliet?
questions.fact: Shakespeare also wrote 154 poems called sonnets.

questions.q: What was the name of the London theater where many of Shakespeare's plays were performed?
questions.fact: A rebuilt Globe Theatre opened near the original site in 1997.

questions.q: Which Portuguese explorer reached India by sailing around Africa in 1498?
questions.fact: Vasco da Gama's route let Europeans trade for spices without crossing land.

questions.q: Which country paid for Christopher Columbus's voyage in 1492?
questions.fact: Queen Isabella and King Ferdinand of Spain agreed to pay for the trip after Portugal said no.

questions.q: What was the name of the ship that carried the Pilgrims to America in 1620?
questions.fact: The Pilgrims founded Plymouth Colony in what is now Massachusetts.

questions.q: What was the first permanent English settlement in North America?
questions.fact: Jamestown was founded in Virginia in 1607.

questions.q: Which English colony is known as the Lost Colony because its settlers vanished?
questions.fact: When help finally arrived, the only clue was the word "CROATOAN" carved into a post.

questions.q: Which Powhatan woman is famous for her connection to the Jamestown colonists?
questions.fact: Pocahontas later traveled to England, where she died in 1617.

questions.q: In what year was the US Declaration of Independence adopted?

questions.q: In 1773, what did American colonists dump into Boston Harbor to protest taxes?
questions.fact: Colonists threw 342 chests of British tea into the water during the Boston Tea Party.

questions.q: Who made a famous midnight ride in 1775 to warn that British soldiers were coming?
questions.fact: Paul Revere was a silversmith, and other riders also helped spread the warning that night.

questions.q: Who commanded the Continental Army during the American Revolution?
questions.fact: Washington spent the hard winter of 1777 to 1778 with his troops at Valley Forge.

questions.q: Which country gave the Statue of Liberty to the United States as a gift?
questions.fact: The statue was shipped across the ocean in 350 pieces and dedicated in 1886.

questions.q: Which famous American document begins with the words "We the People"?

questions.q: What are the first ten amendments to the US Constitution called?
questions.fact: The Bill of Rights protects freedoms like free speech and freedom of religion.

questions.q: Which US president bought the huge Louisiana Territory from France in 1803?

questions.q: Which two explorers led an expedition across the American West starting in 1804?

questions.q: Who was the US president during the American Civil War?

questions.q: Which famous Lincoln speech begins with "Four score and seven years ago"?
questions.fact: The Gettysburg Address is fewer than 300 words long and took about two minutes to give.

questions.q: In what year did the American Civil War end?

questions.q: Which woman escaped slavery and then led many others to freedom on the Underground Railroad?
questions.fact: Harriet Tubman made about 13 trips and guided around 70 people to freedom.

questions.q: Which man escaped slavery and became a famous speaker and writer against it?
questions.fact: Frederick Douglass taught himself to read even though it was illegal for enslaved people.

questions.q: In which US state did a famous gold rush begin in 1848?

questions.q: What was the name of the long trail many pioneers used to travel west by wagon in the 1800s?

questions.q: In what year was the first railroad across the United States completed?

questions.q: Which woman refused to give up her bus seat in Montgomery, Alabama, in 1955?

questions.q: Which country did the United States buy Alaska from in 1867?

questions.q: What 1929 event helped start the Great Depression?

questions.q: Which US president created the New Deal programs during the Great Depression?

questions.q: In what year did World War I end?

questions.q: What were the long ditches that soldiers fought from in World War I called?
questions.fact: The strip of land between enemy trenches was called No Man's Land.

questions.q: In what year did World War II begin?
questions.fact: The war started in Europe when Germany invaded Poland on September 1, 1939.

questions.q: Which attack on December 7, 1941 brought the United States into World War II?
questions.fact: Pearl Harbor is a naval base in Hawaii.

questions.q: What was the code name for the Allied invasion of Normandy in 1944?

questions.q: Who was the British prime minister for most of World War II?
questions.fact: Churchill was also a painter and won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1953.

questions.q: Which Jewish girl wrote a diary while hiding from the Nazis in Amsterdam?
